analysis.notes: Workshop report (Werkstattbericht) with three teaching scenarios in social work higher education. Prompting competence is treated as learning content, a declared prompting appendix and Chain-of-Thought prompting are recommended; Role_Persona rests on the role play in which ChatGPT simulates a help-seeking person. Bias is named generically (normierendes und diskriminierendes Potenzial) without an axis or a harm mechanism for the work's own object. The 'Verzerrungen' in the role play scenario concern realism of the simulated client, not social bias. Mitigation is the proposed curricular embedding of the discriminatory potential in teaching. Rammert's technology theory frames AI as an actor, not gender or bias.

evidence.snippet: GPT-4o fed the Vasquez definition of heteronormativity along with three annotated examples (Prompt 1).

analysis.notes: Experiments on the emotional content of responses of seven LLMs to heteronormative versus non-heteronormative prompts and to LGBTQ+ slang. Axes: queer identity expressed through language (Sexual_Orientation_Identity) and queer slang as a language variety, 'minority slangs and argots' (Language_Culture). The more negative emotion labels for queer slang are a difference in tone and are therefore not coded as Disparate_Performance; Exclusionary_Norms rests on the work's own result and argument that guardrails against heteronormative language leave a bias against queer language. Bias definition: the adopted Vasquez definition determines heteronormative language as the input category of the experiments; LLM bias itself is recognisable only from the measurement of disproportionately negative emotional labels, so Implicit_Only. Existing safety guardrails are inferred from response patterns and are not an identified or assessed mitigation, so mitigation is None. Gender understanding: the heteronormativity frame treats traditional gender roles, binary gender norms and cisnormativity as normative orders encoded in language, which is taken as the explicit statement for Social_Construct; this is a boundary case under codebook 1.4.1 and is flagged. Theory reference: the heteronormativity taxonomy of Marchia and Sommer with the definition of Vasquez et al. ICL: GPT-4o tagging prompt with definition and three annotated examples.

Axes: queer identity expressed through language (Sexual_Orientation_Identity) and queer slang as a language variety, 'minority slangs and argots' (Language_Culture). The more negative emotion labels for queer slang are a difference in tone and are therefore not coded as Disparate_Performance; Exclusionary_Norms rests on the work's own result and argument that guardrails against heteronormative language leave a bias against queer language. Bias definition: the adopted Vasquez definition determines heteronormative language as the input category of the experiments; LLM bias itself is recognisable only from the measurement of disproportionately negative emotional labels, so Implicit_Only. Existing safety guardrails are inferred from response patterns and are not an identified or assessed mitigation, so mitigation is None. Gender understanding: the heteronormativity frame treats traditional gender roles, binary gender norms and cisnormativity as normative orders encoded in language, which is taken as the explicit statement for Social_Construct; this is a boundary case under codebook 1.4.1 and is flagged. analysis.notes: Formal hypercube framework for intersectional fairness with proofs, a variance-based metric family (VarRatio) and verification on synthetic data and the Adult dataset. Studientyp Konzept: the core contribution is the framework, the propagation algorithm and the metrics; the synthetic and real-data experiments serve to verify the theoretical results. Gender, ethnicity and age are the work's own worked examples and the Adult protected attributes (marital status is a further attribute, not coded as a social axis of disadvantage). Indirect_Discrimination: the work defines worst case disparate impact and statistical parity for the outcomes of a binary classification, proves their propagation and finds intersectional bias in Adult; the classification follows the work's own use of disparate impact. Disparate_Performance: section 4.2 and Appendix B extend the framework to Equality of Opportunity, 'that seek to equalize the performance of our model on different subgroups', and prove that worst case accuracy, precision and error-rate disparities narrow up the levels; this rests on the work's own derivation and is not measured empirically. Gender is binary by construction (binary protected attributes, male/female). No mitigation is applied; bottom-up fairness is a design principle without a stage. Theory reference: Crenshaw's intersectionality from Black feminist scholarship frames the problem.

analysis.notes: Narrative review of AI in social sciences and social work 2022 to 2025. The synthesis has its own section 'Algorithmic Discrimination and Bias' and case-study section; axes coded from these: race (COMPAS) and low income (child-welfare flagging, Robodebt). Disability and single mothers appear in one sentence on French welfare litigation only. Indirect_Discrimination: allocation decisions (child-welfare flagging, debt notices, risk scores) that disadvantage groups through historical training data and data matching, without the group attribute as decision criterion; the work does not itself classify direct or indirect. Mitigation: diverse training datasets (Pre_Processing), adversarial debiasing and fairness constraints (In_Training), human oversight, bias audits and collaborative governance (Organisational_Process); the review reports these as implemented in pilot programmes without a reported result, hence Demonstrated. Source-quality note: several references carry placeholder URLs ('xxxx') and implausible bibliographic data, flagged for the domain experts; codes rely only on the work's own statements. AI Agent Review: Health_Care is kept because section 3.3 addresses health monitoring, telemedicine and virtual nursing in disability and elderly care as a field of the review.

analysis.notes: Narrative review of AI in social sciences and social work 2022 to 2025. The synthesis has its own section 'Algorithmic Discrimination and Bias' and case-study section; axes coded from these: race (COMPAS) and low income (child-welfare flagging, Robodebt). Disability and single mothers appear in one sentence on French welfare litigation only. Indirect_Discrimination: allocation decisions (child-welfare flagging, debt notices, risk scores) that disadvantage groups through historical training data and data matching, without the group attribute as decision criterion; the work does not itself classify direct or indirect. Mitigation: diverse training datasets (Pre_Processing), adversarial debiasing and fairness constraints (In_Training), human oversight, bias audits and collaborative governance (Organisational_Process); the review reports these as implemented in pilot programmes without a reported result, hence Demonstrated. Source-quality note: several references carry placeholder URLs ('xxxx') and implausible bibliographic data, flagged for the domain experts; codes rely only on the work's own statements. AI Agent Review: Health_Care is kept because section 3.3 addresses health monitoring, telemedicine and virtual nursing in disability and elderly care as a field of the review.

analysis.notes: Critical survey and typology of feminist AI (model, design, policy, discourse, culture, science). Bias axes gender and race carry the work's own argument on technoliberal inclusion and racial capitalism; class and LGBTQI+ appear in enumerations. Intersectional left uncoded: intersectionality is named as a strand of feminism, the combination examples (facial recognition, Sinders data set) are reported from other work. AN_Harm_Types None: 'male as norm', stereotyped word embeddings and gender-bias norms are reported positions of cited authors, the typology is not structured by harm types. Mitigation: Sinders' bias-correcting data collection (Pre_Processing) and participatory design in Poieto (Organisational_Process) are reported as applied in small projects without evaluation, hence Demonstrated, a synthesised status. Social_Construct rests on the adopted feminist STS frame and Wajcman's 'historical and cultural construction of gender'; gender is not defined in an own sentence. AI Agent Review: AN_Task None, because the work types conceptions of feminist AI; the legal knowledge prototype, the court transparency system and the Mumkin chatbot are reported projects illustrating the typology, not a task of professional practice for which the work itself describes or proposes AI use.

Section 5.2 and Table 3 assess a CoT prompting comparator (Prompt_Practice) and criticise prompt sensitivity and demographic generalisation. Prompting is Research_Instrument and Object_of_Critique. analysis.notes: Experiment on Flan-PaLM 540B with a people-diversity dataset (105 professions) and a culture-diversity dataset, automated entropy and max-gap metrics and human side-by-side ratings. CCSV combines self-critique and revision (Self_Criticism) with sampling several drafts and self-voting (Ensembling); the baselines comprise 5-shot exemplars (ICL), zero- and few-shot chain-of-thought (Thought_Generation) and the 0-shot instruction 'Write AI model's response to the user question such that it has diversity' (General_Guidance), which failed. Evaluated: CCSV outperforms all baselines on automated and human evaluation (Sections 5.1, 6). Fine-tuning with CCSV data is named only as future work and not coded as In_Training. Language_Culture through the culture-diversity task rated by humans (Section 6.2). Erasure: under-representation or erasure of demographic groups in the responses, measured as entropy close to 0. Exclusionary_Norms: the work's own baseline output defaults to 'only white male CEOs' when the prompt is under-specified, which the work attributes to implicit assumptions of the model (Abstract, Section 1). AN_Gender_Understanding Binary_Categorical with Implicit_Only: the analysis uses fixed knowledge-graph labels male, female and other, and the work itself states that 'other' is not an ideal stand-in for genders beyond male and female and that the gender signal is incomplete (footnote 2, Limitations), so no gender beyond the binary is a category of the analysis; boundary case for the domain experts. analysis.notes: Conceptual paper that rearticulates the seven data feminism principles for AI research and proposes two further principles (environment, consent); the appendix calls it primarily a literature review and theory contribution, coded Konzept because the principles form a framework. Other_Axis: colonial Global North/Global South position, argued in Principle 7 (labour hierarchy) and 5.1 (environmental impact). Harm types: Exclusionary_Norms for the gender binary operationalised in AI research (4.3), Erasure for missing data on groups and the erasure of trans and non-binary people (4.1, 4.3), Indirect_Discrimination for tenant screening on eviction records, arrest records and credit scores that disproportionately impacts people of color (4.1); harms such as Gender Shades, LAION misogyny or anti-Muslim LLM bias are cited from other work and left uncoded. Mitigation: collection of missing data on underrepresented people (Pre_Processing) and participatory methods, AI education, regulation and collective action (Organisational_Process), all proposed. Bias is not determined in a sentence of its own; the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame (Implicit_Only). Fairness nein: the paper frames its argument as justice and power, not as algorithmic fairness criteria or metrics. AI Agent Review: Generative_KI is teilweise because the work addresses AI research in general and treats generative models as one recurring strand beside predictive AI ('These evaluations are necessary for both generative and predictive AI'). AN_Bias_Definition is Implicit_Only because the adopted definition in Principle 1 determines power, not bias, discrimination or unfairness, and the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame only. The intersectional bias-axis passage of Principle 1 and the status-quo passage of Principle 2 for Exclusionary_Norms were added from the other track.

analysis.notes: Theoretische Analyse mit Literaturreview, Hauptbeitrag ist ein rechtebasiertes Rahmenwerk aus vier Komponenten (ethische AI Literacy, partizipative Governance, kontinuierliche Folgenabschätzung, gemeinwesenorientierte Advocacy) mit Empfehlungen in Tabelle 1, daher Studientyp Konzept. Generative KI wird nicht behandelt. AN_Bias_Axes Socioeconomic und AN_Harm_Types Indirect_Discrimination aus dem im eigenen Argument zu Groupthink ausgeführten Fall eines Risikoinstruments der Kinder- und Jugendhilfe, das armutsbezogene Faktoren als Missbrauchsindikatoren wertete. Grenzfall, weil der Fall aus der Literatur übernommen ist. Erasure aus dem eigenen Argument zur epistemischen Ungerechtigkeit, nach dem Algorithmen das Erfahrungswissen marginalisierter Gemeinschaften diskontieren. Rassismus erscheint nur in einer Policy-Empfehlung und in Fallnennungen, nicht als analysierte Achse. Alle Maßnahmen sind organisatorisch und vorgeschlagen (Schulung, Supervision, Beteiligung, Audit, Monitoring), das empirische Testen des Rahmenwerks steht in den Limitationen als offene Aufgabe. Bias wird über strukturelle Ungleichheit und differenzielle Wirkungen gerahmt, ohne eigene Bestimmung. Theoriebezug über epistemische Ungerechtigkeit nach Fricker, TAM, I-C-E-Modell und sozioökologische Systemtheorie rahmen Technikakzeptanz und Implementierung, nicht Bias. Geschlecht wird nicht behandelt.

analysis.notes: Theoretische Analyse mit Literaturreview, Hauptbeitrag ist ein rechtebasiertes Rahmenwerk aus vier Komponenten (ethische AI Literacy, partizipative Governance, kontinuierliche Folgenabschätzung, gemeinwesenorientierte Advocacy) mit Empfehlungen in Tabelle 1, daher Studientyp Konzept. Generative KI wird nicht behandelt. AN_Bias_Axes Socioeconomic und AN_Harm_Types Indirect_Discrimination aus dem im eigenen Argument zu Groupthink ausgeführten Fall eines Risikoinstruments der Kinder- und Jugendhilfe, das armutsbezogene Faktoren als Missbrauchsindikatoren wertete. Grenzfall, weil der Fall aus der Literatur übernommen ist. Erasure aus dem eigenen Argument zur epistemischen Ungerechtigkeit, nach dem Algorithmen das Erfahrungswissen marginalisierter Gemeinschaften diskontieren. Rassismus erscheint nur in einer Policy-Empfehlung und in Fallnennungen, nicht als analysierte Achse. Alle Maßnahmen sind organisatorisch und vorgeschlagen (Schulung, Supervision, Beteiligung, Audit, Monitoring), das empirische Testen des Rahmenwerks steht in den Limitationen als offene Aufgabe. Bias wird über strukturelle Ungleichheit und differenzielle Wirkungen gerahmt, ohne eigene Bestimmung. Theoriebezug über epistemische Ungerechtigkeit nach Fricker, TAM, I-C-E-Modell und sozioökologische Systemtheorie rahmen Technikakzeptanz und Implementierung, nicht Bias. Geschlecht wird nicht behandelt.

evidence.snippet: We demonstrate how imagery produced through SD perpetuates pre-existing power systems such as sexism, racism, heteronormativity, and ableism, and assumes a default individual as white, able-bodied, and masculine-presenting.

evidence.snippet: Through this, we urge reflection on embedding anti-oppressive, anti-structural forces in technology design, and suggest potential ways forward through an intersectional feminist approach requiring dialogue between academia, industry, creative practitioners, an

evidence.term: Across various images, gender assignments were automatically applied by SDXL, re
evidence.snippet: Across various images, gender assignments were automatically applied by SDXL, resulting in aesthetics that excluded feminine or non-binary representations.

evidence.term: In this paper, we critically analyze Stable Diffusion (SD), a widely used open-s
evidence.snippet: In this paper, we critically analyze Stable Diffusion (SD), a widely used open-source vGenAI tool, through visual and intersectional analysis.

evidence.term: When it came to the visual images, we used a specific prompting strategy to prod
evidence.snippet: When it came to the visual images, we used a specific prompting strategy to produce a dataset comprising 180 images using SDXL.

evidence.term: By keeping prompts minimal, we aimed to observe the default outputs and hegemoni
evidence.snippet: By keeping prompts minimal, we aimed to observe the default outputs and hegemonic aesthetics in the imagery.

analysis.notes: Interpretative qualitative visual and intersectional analysis of 180 Stable Diffusion XL images from 18 deliberately minimal prompts (privilege and discrimination, ideology, everyday scenarios) on micro, meso and macro levels, complemented by a review of online and academic sources. Prompts serve as research instrument; minimal prompts simulate everyday internet users without prompt-engineering knowledge. General_Guidance, verbatim strategy: users 'being more conscious of how they are generating images-e.g. what kind of prompts they use, and what kind of aesthetics they pick into the images'. AN_Task = None: the work audits default image outputs of the tool for everyday users and tests no professional application task; creative and design practice of artists appears as context and addressee of recommendations in the discussion. Axes from the own image analysis: gender, skin tone and ethnicity, disability, body size, age, wealth and class, immigrant/refugee versus citizen, Global North cultural hegemony, heteronormativity and absent non-binary representations; Intersectional from the micro-level analysis of the white, adult, able-bodied, heteronormative masculine default and single-axis diversification. Religion was excluded from the scope by the authors. Harm types: stereotyping, exclusion of feminine, non-binary and disabled representations (Erasure), white able-bodied masculine and Global North default (Exclusionary_Norms), reductionist portrayal of cultures and the Global South as poor (Misrepresentation). The confederate-flag finding concerns imagery, not language, so Toxicity is not coded. Mitigation only proposed within algorithmic reparation: curated training data (Pre_Processing), conscious prompting by users (Prompt_Practice), responsible designers, diverse teams, regulation and criminal culpability (Organisational_Process). Gender definition from footnote 2, which defines the binary gender norm and replaces man/woman by heteronormative feminine/masculine representations; it is a terminological determination rather than a definition of gender in the narrow sense.

evidence.term: A key factor here is that experts also acquire knowledge of topics outside their
evidence.snippet: A key factor here is that experts also acquire knowledge of topics outside their field, so that technicians, for example, also deal with legal issues and lawyers acquire basic knowledge of data processing and data science methods.

evidence.term: Here, bias refers to the presence of systematic and unfair behaviour and errors
evidence.snippet: Here, bias refers to the presence of systematic and unfair behaviour and errors in AI systems. Hence, a bias may lead to discriminatory outcomes and unfair treatment, which further implicates the importance of fairness.

evidence.term: Representation bias arises from the manner of data sampling from a population. T
evidence.snippet: Representation bias arises from the manner of data sampling from a population. This results in nonrepresentative samples or unbalanced data with a lack of diversity, missing subgroups or other anomalies [109].

evidence.term: Although there is a certain affinity between the terms diversity, non-discrimina
evidence.snippet: Although there is a certain affinity between the terms diversity, non-discrimination and fairness, they are associated with other different aspects which are not identical.

evidence.term: This results in nonrepresentative samples or unbalanced data with a lack of dive
evidence.snippet: This results in nonrepresentative samples or unbalanced data with a lack of diversity, missing subgroups or other anomalies [109].

evidence.term: In our research, we primarily concentrate on aspects of non-discrimination, enco
evidence.snippet: In our research, we primarily concentrate on aspects of non-discrimination, encompassing both group and individual fairness.

evidence.term: The main distinction between those measurements is the differentiation into grou
evidence.snippet: The main distinction between those measurements is the differentiation into group fairness and individual fairness.

evidence.term: For example, consider a hiring algorithm and the underlying dataset. If there ar
evidence.snippet: For example, consider a hiring algorithm and the underlying dataset. If there are more males than females present in the training set, the dataset is unbalanced and might result in a disadvantage of females, while promoting males.

evidence.term: Group fairness is based on statistical parity between certain groups (e.g. gende
evidence.snippet: Group fairness is based on statistical parity between certain groups (e.g. gender, age, and race). This becomes clear when, for example, women always get a different result than men or young people are favoured over older people.

evidence.term: It should also be kept in mind that there are situations in which group fairness
evidence.snippet: It should also be kept in mind that there are situations in which group fairness leads to better results, in comparison to individual fairness. This is evident in socio-political issues such as gender equality.

evidence.term: Basically, ChatGPT is a Large Language Model (LLM), which is pre-trained by huge
evidence.snippet: Basically, ChatGPT is a Large Language Model (LLM), which is pre-trained by huge amounts of data, such as webpages, books or other written material and deployed as a conversational AI system.

evidence.term: In addition, these models are by no means immune to bias.
evidence.snippet: In addition, these models are by no means immune to bias.

evidence.term: To address this issue, this paper investigates current state-ofthe-art methods f
evidence.snippet: To address this issue, this paper investigates current state-ofthe-art methods for bias mitigation and contrasts them with the legal requirements, with the scope limited to the European Union and with a particular focus on the AI Act.

evidence.term: Bias mitigation techniques can be applied in various stages of the machine learn
evidence.snippet: Bias mitigation techniques can be applied in various stages of the machine learning pipeline, e.g., data collection, pre-processing, inprocessing, post-processing, or even after evaluating a machine-made decision [113].

analysis.notes: Interdisziplinäre rechtlich-technische Analyse, die Fairnessmaße und Verfahren der Bias-Minderung mit EU-Recht und AI Act kontrastiert und individuelle Fairness als rechtlich passenderes Konzept begründet, keine eigene Datenerhebung. Studientyp Theoretisch, weil das Werk ohne Suchmethode referiert und argumentativ schließt. AN_Bias_Axes Gender und Race_Ethnicity aus eigenen Arbeitsbeispielen (Datenaugmentation durch Geschlechtertausch, Kreditvergabe an zwei ethnische Gruppen), Intersectional aus dem Abschnitt zu Gruppen an der Schnittstelle zweier Achsen und der eigenen Kritik, dass das EU-Recht Diskriminierungsgründe nur einzeln betrachtet. Socioeconomic bleibt uncodiert, wirtschaftlicher oder sozialer Status steht nur als Aufzählung. AN_Harm_Types Direct_Discrimination und Indirect_Discrimination, weil das Werk Diskriminierung selbst als unmittelbar und mittelbar einschließlich Proxy-Diskriminierung klassifiziert. Disparate_Performance nicht codiert, die Fehlerratenvergleiche sind Fairnesskriterien und der einzige Qualitätsunterschied zwischen Gruppen ist das zitierte Ergebnis von Buolamwini und Gebru. AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated gilt nur für das synthetisierte Ergebnis von Tyagi et al. (erweiterter Variational Autoencoder mindert Gender-Bias statischer Worteinbettungen), alle übrigen Verfahren und die Empfehlungen zu Audits, Dokumentation und interdisziplinären Teams sind Inventar oder Vorschlag. Geschlecht erscheint nur binär in Beispielen, ohne eigene Bestimmung. Theoriebezug über prozedurale Fairness nach Tyler, die rechtliche Unterscheidung unmittelbarer und mittelbarer Diskriminierung und individuelle Fairness nach Dwork et al.

evidence.snippet: Using AI in health care as a case study, we argue that AI bias is a form of structural injustice that exists when AI systems interact with other social factors to exacerbate existing social inequalities

(2021): patientenberichtete Schmerzwerte als Label und diverser Datensatz (Pre_Processing) senken unerklärte Schmerzdisparitäten; keine eigene Evaluation. evidence.snippet: These tasks are related to distribution, indicating that ChatGPT has cultural biases in distributive fairness.

evidence.snippet: This can help us understand ChatGPT ' s perception of individuals from different countries and assess whether they hold cultural stereotypes.

evidence.snippet: This approach would facilitate more effective and respectful cross-cultural interactions.

evidence.snippet: While both models display cultural bias, ChatGPT 4o exhibits it in fewer tasks, suggesting improved fairness in interactions

evidence.term: Given the rapid advancement of large-scale language models, AI models, like Chat
evidence.snippet: Given the rapid advancement of large-scale language models, AI models, like ChatGPT, are playing an increasingly prominent role in human society.

evidence.term: Furthermore, Study 3 created four kinds of prompt strategies and applied them to
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, Study 3 created four kinds of prompt strategies and applied them to decision-making tasks.

evidence.term: It also found that the four prompt strategies can effectively reduce the generat
evidence.snippet: It also found that the four prompt strategies can effectively reduce the generation of ChatGPT ' s stereotypes and biases.

analysis.notes: Three studies with ChatGPT 3.5 and 4o: cultural value scales (Study 1), 13 one-round decision tasks with country personas and country interactants (Study 2), four prompt strategies as intervention (Study 3). Role_Persona: 'If you are an ordinary individual from [the country]' as instrument; General_Guidance covers the debiasing cues 'From a fairness perspective,', 'As an independent individual, please make a choice according to your own ideas and', 'If you live in a future world.' and 'Imagine you live in a multicultural world,'. Evaluated: the prompt strategies reduced country differences to non-significance in most tested task-model combinations, but the personal-preference prompt failed in the GPT-4o public goods game (own experiment). Axes coded as the work names them, countries/nationality and cultural groups. Direct_Discrimination: allocation decisions (dictator, ultimatum, public goods) toward interactants vary with the nationality stated in the prompt; these are simulated game allocations, not real decisions about persons. Training-data and oversight recommendations in the discussion are outlook and not coded as stages. Theory: Hofstede's cultural dimensions and GLOBE dimensions frame the explanation of the bias sources. Gender appears only as the GLOBE dimension gender egalitarianism, not as an object. Review: Diversitaet teilweise, weil das Werk die Wahrnehmung von Personen aus 20 Laendern und einen respektvollen interkulturellen Umgang als nachgeordneten Teilaspekt behandelt. Direct_Discrimination beruht auf simulierten Zuteilungen im Spiel und bleibt ein Grenzfall fuer die Fachpruefung.

records.authors: Salinas, A.; Haim, A.; Nyarko, J.

evidence.term: We find that the advice systematically disadvantages names that are commonly ass
evidence.snippet: We find that the advice systematically disadvantages names that are commonly associated with racial minorities and women.

evidence.term: But because names strongly correlate with race/gender, any disparities we observ
evidence.snippet: But because names strongly correlate with race/gender, any disparities we observe may constitute bias in the form of disparate impact.

evidence.term: The audit we conducted is cost-effective to implement, and thus could be recomme
evidence.snippet: The audit we conducted is cost-effective to implement, and thus could be recommended as part of a routine due diligence process before models are released.

evidence.term: Similarly, female-perceived names yield systematically worse outcomes than male-
evidence.snippet: Similarly, female-perceived names yield systematically worse outcomes than male-perceived names.

evidence.term: We employ an audit design to investigate biases in state-of-the-art large langua
evidence.snippet: We employ an audit design to investigate biases in state-of-the-art large language models, including GPT-4.

evidence.term: While providing numerical, decision-relevant anchors in the prompt can successfu
evidence.snippet: While providing numerical, decision-relevant anchors in the prompt can successfully counteract the biases, qualitative details have inconsistent effects and may even increase disparities.

evidence.term: Our approach also allows us to assess the sensitivity of biases to certain desig
evidence.snippet: Our approach also allows us to assess the sensitivity of biases to certain design features of the prompt.

analysis.notes: Audit study with 42 prompt templates in five scenarios (purchase, chess, public office, sports, hiring) and 40 first names perceived as Black or white and male or female, 100 repetitions each, on GPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Llama-3-70B, Mistral Large and PaLM-2. Prompts are the research instrument, and the three context levels test prompt design. General_Guidance, verbatim strategy: 'providing the model with a numeric anchor' (decision-relevant numeric information in the prompt), which the work's own experiment shows to remove name-based disparities in most scenarios, while qualitative context has inconsistent effects (Prompt_Practice, Evaluated); routine audits at deployment and implementation are recommended (Organisational_Process, Proposed). Other_Task: advice to laypeople in negotiation, hiring salary offers, election and sports predictions, outside social work. Intersectional is coded under the AN_Bias_Axes rule because Black female-perceived names yield the worst outcomes compared with Black and with female names, although the authors state that this analysis does not equate to an evaluation of intersectionality. Harm type: Indirect_Discrimination following the codebook anchor, since names act as proxies in numeric advice about persons (offers, salaries, chances) and the work interprets the disparities as disparate impact. The outputs are allocative decisions, not depictions of groups, and the encoded stereotypes are the authors' explanation of the mechanism; Stereotyping is therefore not coded as a separate representational harm. Gender is operationalised through male- and female-perceived names without definition. Bias is defined through the legal pair of disparate treatment and disparate impact, which also frames the interpretation (theory reference, a boundary case between legal doctrine and theory).

evidence.term: We find that the advice systematically disadvantages names that are commonly ass
evidence.snippet: We find that the advice systematically disadvantages names that are commonly associated with racial minorities and women.

evidence.term: But because names strongly correlate with race/gender, any disparities we observ
evidence.snippet: But because names strongly correlate with race/gender, any disparities we observe may constitute bias in the form of disparate impact.

evidence.term: The audit we conducted is cost-effective to implement, and thus could be recomme
evidence.snippet: The audit we conducted is cost-effective to implement, and thus could be recommended as part of a routine due diligence process before models are released.

evidence.term: Similarly, female-perceived names yield systematically worse outcomes than male-
evidence.snippet: Similarly, female-perceived names yield systematically worse outcomes than male-perceived names.

evidence.term: We employ an audit design to investigate biases in state-of-the-art large langua
evidence.snippet: We employ an audit design to investigate biases in state-of-the-art large language models, including GPT-4.

evidence.term: While providing numerical, decision-relevant anchors in the prompt can successfu
evidence.snippet: While providing numerical, decision-relevant anchors in the prompt can successfully counteract the biases, qualitative details have inconsistent effects and may even increase disparities.

evidence.term: Our approach also allows us to assess the sensitivity of biases to certain desig
evidence.snippet: Our approach also allows us to assess the sensitivity of biases to certain design features of the prompt.

analysis.notes: Audit study with 42 prompt templates in five scenarios (purchase, chess, public office, sports, hiring) and 40 first names perceived as Black or white and male or female, 100 repetitions each, on GPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Llama-3-70B, Mistral Large and PaLM-2. Prompts are the research instrument, and the three context levels test prompt design. General_Guidance, verbatim strategy: 'providing the model with a numeric anchor' (decision-relevant numeric information in the prompt), which the work's own experiment shows to remove name-based disparities in most scenarios, while qualitative context has inconsistent effects (Prompt_Practice, Evaluated); routine audits at deployment and implementation are recommended (Organisational_Process, Proposed). Other_Task: advice to laypeople in negotiation, hiring salary offers, election and sports predictions, outside social work. Intersectional is coded under the AN_Bias_Axes rule because Black female-perceived names yield the worst outcomes compared with Black and with female names, although the authors state that this analysis does not equate to an evaluation of intersectionality. Harm type: Indirect_Discrimination following the codebook anchor, since names act as proxies in numeric advice about persons (offers, salaries, chances) and the work interprets the disparities as disparate impact. The outputs are allocative decisions, not depictions of groups, and the encoded stereotypes are the authors' explanation of the mechanism; Stereotyping is therefore not coded as a separate representational harm. Gender is operationalised through male- and female-perceived names without definition. Bias is defined through the legal pair of disparate treatment and disparate impact, which also frames the interpretation (theory reference, a boundary case between legal doctrine and theory).

records.authors: Clemmer, C.; Ding, J.; Feng, Y.

evidence.snippet: Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of PreciseDebias in rectifying biases pertaining to both ethnicity and gender in images.

evidence.term: PreciseDebias can diversify the racial profiles in generated images by adeptly a
evidence.snippet: PreciseDebias can diversify the racial profiles in generated images by adeptly augmenting such generic text prompts

evidence.term: Relevant studies, including [5,11,13], modified or fine-tuned predictions based
evidence.snippet: Relevant studies, including [5,11,13], modified or fine-tuned predictions based on specific fairness criteria after the model has been trained. The method proposed in this paper is classified within the post-processing category.

evidence.term: Figure 3c shows how the discrepancy in gender distributions between the generate
evidence.snippet: Figure 3c shows how the discrepancy in gender distributions between the generated images and the ground truth narrows with an increased number of training interactions.

evidence.term: In this paper, we propose PreciseDebias, a comprehensive end-to-end framework th
evidence.snippet: In this paper, we propose PreciseDebias, a comprehensive end-to-end framework that can rectify demographic bias in image generation.

evidence.term: PreciseDebias transforms generic text prompts to produce images in line with spe
evidence.snippet: PreciseDebias transforms generic text prompts to produce images in line with specified demographic distributions.

analysis.notes: Debiasing framework for text-to-image generation in which a fine-tuned LLM rewrites generic prompts to match target demographic distributions; evaluated against ground-truth ratios and regex and NER baselines. General_Guidance strategy, verbatim: 'transform generic prompts devoid of demographic specifics into those that are demographically informed'. ICL: few-shot prompting of GPT-3 for training data. Mitigation stages: Prompt_Practice for the rewriting of prompts before a frozen image model, and In_Training for the proportional fine-tuning of the rewriting LLM with learning rates scaled by the measured bias per demographic characteristic (section 3.2.4, Algorithms 2 and 3). The work classifies its method as post-processing, but it changes no output of the image model, so Post_Processing is not coded. Status Evaluated: the reduction of the gap between generated and target ratios for ethnicity and gender is reported. Exclusionary_Norms rests on the work's own observation that generic prompts default to White subjects and prioritise certain groups. Gender is analysed as male and female; the limitation sentence that gender should not be confined to the binary does not change the analysis.

evidence.snippet: In this research paper, we offer a methodology, which we call inclusive prompt engineering, to describe the process of examining and modifying the relationship between written prompts and visual outputs of human subjects using AI.

evidence.term: Through a series of prompt engineering practices, we show how users can bypass t
evidence.snippet: Through a series of prompt engineering practices, we show how users can bypass this toxic positivity to create images that better demonstrate the diversity of humanity, including a range of ages, body sizes, races, and genders.

analysis.notes: General_Guidance: den von DALL-E zurueckgegebenen Prompt als Vorlage nutzen, wichtige Merkmale mehrfach mit Synonymen verstaerken und negative Merkmale positiv formulieren ('reinforcing particularly important traits several times with various synonyms'); Zero-Shot-Prompts dienen als Basislinie. Other_Task: Erstellung von Bildern fuer Content Design und technische Kommunikation (Social-Media-Kampagnen, Interfaces, Personas). Achsen aus eigenen Fallbeispielen: Low-Income-Paar (Socioeconomic, Race_Ethnicity), aeltere Frau (Age), Koerpergewicht und Glatze (Physical_Appearance), Disability im eigenen Argument zur toxic positivity, maennlicher Default (Gender). Demonstrated: Methode an Beispielen vorgefuehrt, ohne abgeschlossene Pruefung. Gender erscheint nur als Diversitaetsmerkmal ohne erkennbares Verstaendnis. Review: Gender bleibt Absent und Unclear, weil das Werk keine Passage enthaelt, die Geschlecht auf zwei Kategorien festlegt. Mann und Frau erscheinen nur als einzelne Bildbeschreibungen, und das Ziel nennt offen "a range of ages, body sizes, races, and genders".

analysis.notes: Practice guide for managers and staff in small and medium enterprises with the KI-FAIRNESS prompting framework, organisational measures and own image-prompt trials in DALL-E 2 and Midjourney. Publication type admitted as scholarly grey literature (university publisher, named authorship, source list, expert contributions), flagged for the domain experts. Other_Task: drafting job advertisements, recommendation letters and company images in HR and marketing. General_Guidance strategy, verbatim: 'Es könnte z.B. explizit gefordert werden, dass Frauen und Männer, Menschen unterschiedlicher Hautfarbe und sozialer Schicht dargestellt werden sollen.' Further strategies: choose the context deliberately, prompt in English ('female and male bosses'), weigh neutrality against explicit diversity, omit gender in recommendation letters or use a 'Verwirrungstaktik', anonymise. Bias axes and harm types rest on the guide's own image-prompt observations and its own job-advertisement argument (Indirect_Discrimination: job-advertisement language that appeals to men deters women and is perpetuated by training); cited news cases are not used. Mitigation status Evaluated applies only to adding 'divers' to the prompt, whose effect is tested in two tools and reported as small; the trial is informal (one prompt), and the other measures (data diversity, targeted training with gender-inclusive terms, governance, training of staff, monitoring, human review) are proposed. Gender understanding: the image analysis contrasts women and men, so Binary_Categorical follows the analysis; the Gender Data Gap remark on genderqueer people, the gender star and 'alle Gender' are conceptual statements that the analysis does not follow. Intersectional rests on the guide's own statement that women and especially Women of Color are sexualised in generated images. Theory reference No: 'Feministische KI' appears only in the outlook as a positive narrative with the MissJourney example, and Data Feminism and the Gender Data Gap appear as further reading or illustration; none of them frames the guide's treatment of gender or bias.

analysis.notes: Survey of bias evaluation metrics, evaluation datasets and mitigation techniques for LLMs with three taxonomies and a harm taxonomy (Table 1). AN_Harm_Types: all nine values structure the survey's own synthesis as rows of Table 1 (representational harms and allocational harms) and, for six of them, as coded columns of Table 4; the Derogatory_Language row label is lost in the conversion of Table 1, so its passage comes from section 2.4.2. AN_Bias_Axes: coded from the targeted-social-group columns of Table 4 (age, gender identity, nationality, physical appearance, race, religion, sexual orientation) and from dialect as the survey's own worked example (African-American English, linguistic profiling); disability and socioeconomic status appear only in dataset enumerations and the 'Other' footnote and are not coded. Intersectional is not coded: the survey argues that group fairness can hold for each group while failing for intersectional subgroups, but names no axis combination whose result it develops. AN_Prompting_Role Research_Instrument: prompt datasets (sentence completions, question answering) are a class of the evaluation taxonomy; modified prompting language is reviewed as a mitigation technique, not recommended. AN_Prompt_Techniques General_Guidance, concrete strategy as synthesised: 'prompting language with different levels of abstraction to instruct the model to avoid using stereotypes' and prepending positive adjectives or phrases to a prompt (section 5.1.4). AN_Mitigation_Stage: the four technical stages are the survey's own taxonomy; Prompt_Practice from modified prompting language; Organisational_Process from participatory research designs, reporting standards and data governance proposed in section 6. AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated as a synthesised evaluation, not the survey's own experiment: the survey reports that Borchers et al. (2022) found instructions prompting diversity or gender equality unsuccessful for bias removal, and that pruning 10-20% of parameters increased resistance to jailbreaking (Hasan, Rugina and Wang 2024); other techniques are inventoried without assessment. AN_Gender_Understanding Social_Construct: the survey states that social groups, which by Definition 3 include gender identity and sex, are socially constructed, contested and tied to power imbalances, and it adopts the critique that binary and immutable gender modelling erases trans, nonbinary and intersex people; its own Figure 1 example uses a male and female substitution. AN_Gender_Definition Implicit_Only because gender itself is not defined. AN_Task None: general LLM bias survey without an application task.

analysis.notes: Research agenda for a feminist metaethics of AI; object is AI ethics as a field, AI in general. Mitigation: proposed research into the diversity of AI ethics boards and the inclusion of those hitherto ignored in decision-making (Organisational_Process, Proposed). AN_Bias_Axes None: gender, class, race, disability and sexuality appear only as a programmatic enumeration and outlook, cited case studies are suggestions, no bias is analysed. AN_Gender_Understanding Intersectional rests on the work's own argument that AI impact is to be examined depending on gender in interaction with other identity markers; boundary case, since the argument is programmatic and no definition of gender is given (Implicit_Only from the intersectional feminist frame). Bias as structural domination and oppression is recognisable from the frame only. AI Agent Review: AN_Bias_Axes stays None because the work analyses no bias along any axis; gender with class, race, disability and sexuality appears as a programmatic research direction of the agenda (Section 3.4) and cited AI cases are illustrative case studies. AN_Gender_Understanding Intersectional is kept from both tracks because the argument of this theoretical work itself makes privilege and disadvantage depend on gender in interaction with other identity markers.

analysis.notes: Research agenda for a feminist metaethics of AI; object is AI ethics as a field, AI in general. Mitigation: proposed research into the diversity of AI ethics boards and the inclusion of those hitherto ignored in decision-making (Organisational_Process, Proposed). AN_Bias_Axes None: gender, class, race, disability and sexuality appear only as a programmatic enumeration and outlook, cited case studies are suggestions, no bias is analysed. AN_Gender_Understanding Intersectional rests on the work's own argument that AI impact is to be examined depending on gender in interaction with other identity markers; boundary case, since the argument is programmatic and no definition of gender is given (Implicit_Only from the intersectional feminist frame). Bias as structural domination and oppression is recognisable from the frame only. AI Agent Review: AN_Bias_Axes stays None because the work analyses no bias along any axis; gender with class, race, disability and sexuality appears as a programmatic research direction of the agenda (Section 3.4) and cited AI cases are illustrative case studies. AN_Gender_Understanding Intersectional is kept from both tracks because the argument of this theoretical work itself makes privilege and disadvantage depend on gender in interaction with other identity markers.

analysis.notes: Theoretical essay that proposes hermeneutic reverse engineering (Balsamo 2011) to examine data and algorithmic bias in AI systems, framed by boundary objects and intersectional feminist thought. AN_Bias_Axes: race and gender are coded from the essay's own sentences that develop the face-detection example (light skin as the norm, 'societal definitions of race and gender'); the opening list of race, gender, ability, language, class, economic background and religion is an enumeration. Sexual_Orientation_Identity is not coded, because gender identity appears only in the single cited Keyes (2018) sentence on automatic gender recognition, which the essay reports and does not develop. Intersectional is not coded, no passage makes an outcome depend on a combination of axes. AN_Harm_Types: Exclusionary_Norms from the essay's own argument on exclusion through hegemonic narration and light skin as the norm, and from its conclusion on questioning what is normal and who falls outside; Erasure from its own finding that questioning data reveals whose cultural narrative is missing. The cited cases of Buolamwini, Noble and Gebru are not coded as harm types. AN_Mitigation_Stage Organisational_Process and AN_Mitigation_Status Proposed: participatory co-design workshops and actionable AI audits are research perspectives, nothing is demonstrated or evaluated. AN_Gender_Understanding Unclear and AN_Gender_Definition Absent: the essay states no understanding of gender of its own; the phrase 'societal definitions of race and gender' attributes the categories to the training of a face-detection system within a cited case and does not state that gender is socially produced, so the Social_Construct threshold of codebook 1.4.1 is not met. AN_Prompting_Role None: observing outputs for different prompts appears once as a cited interrogation idea. AN_Task None: AI is the object of critique, no professional task of AI use is described.

evidence.term: AI literacy includes the knowledge and skills that enable people to critically u
evidence.snippet: AI literacy includes the knowledge and skills that enable people to critically understand, evaluate, and use AI systems and tools to safely and effectively participate in an increasingly digital world.

evidence.term: Underscoring our framework is human judgment and justice, which are core values
evidence.snippet: Underscoring our framework is human judgment and justice, which are core values for applying AI in appropriate contexts and mitigating the harmful effects of algorithms

evidence.term: AI systems are impacting the lives of nearly everyone within modern society, but
evidence.snippet: AI systems are impacting the lives of nearly everyone within modern society, but their results do not equally represent the interests of all people They can and have exacerbated existing oppression and prejudice within society

evidence.term: Inclusivity Elevate the needs, interest, and voice of marginalized communities i
evidence.snippet: Inclusivity Elevate the needs, interest, and voice of marginalized communities in the development of policy and guidance in order to ensure AI tools are accessible to all students and do not perpetuate harmful biases

evidence.term: For example if asked to generate an image of a doctor, a GenAI model might be mo
evidence.snippet: For example if asked to generate an image of a doctor, a GenAI model might be more likely to generate a white male

evidence.term: Generative AI (GenAI) systems and tools are entering the classroom at a rapid pa
evidence.snippet: Generative AI (GenAI) systems and tools are entering the classroom at a rapid pace

evidence.term: Interacting with AI systems is engaging with adaptive technology in multiple mod
evidence.snippet: Interacting with AI systems is engaging with adaptive technology in multiple modalities that adjusts to data collected, such as when learners use adaptive tutors in math or reading to receive content at their level of understanding

evidence.term: The skill of GenAI prompting involves creating good questions or commands that g
evidence.snippet: The skill of GenAI prompting involves creating good questions or commands that get the system to produce something that humans consider to be a quality output

analysis.notes: General_Guidance: 'Effectively prompting a GenAI system or tool takes time and often requires clear communication, specificity, experimentation, and patience' sowie 'Distinguish between essential and nonessential components of a prompt to produce an appropriate output'; Prompt Organizer im Fallbeispiel einer Foerderklasse. AN_Bias_Axes None: Achsen erscheinen in zitierten Beispielen (Druga et al., O'Neil, Buolamwini) und in einem einzelnen, nicht ausgefuehrten Arztbild-Beispiel; Grenzfall nach Anker VSZM7CT6. AN_Harm_Types None: Schadensmechanismen nur aus zitierter Literatur, nicht aus eigenem Argument oder Ergebnis. Organisational_Process: Richtlinien zu Adoption und Evaluation mit Inklusivitaet, professionelles Lernen, Bewusstsein fuer algorithmischen Bias, alles vorgeschlagen. Education_Professional fuer die Fortbildung von Lehrkraeften, Not_SW_Specific fuer K-12-Schueler:innen. Gender erscheint in der eigenen Argumentation nur binaer ("particularly females and students of color" gegenueber "disproportionately enroll white males"), ohne Bestimmung, daher Implicit_Only und Binary_Categorical. Teaching_Further_Education: KI-Nutzung fuer Unterrichtsplanung und Schreibfoerderung.

evidence.snippet: Wenn solche automatisierten und selbstlernenden Systeme eingesetzt werden, kann das zu Diskriminierungen führen sowie bestehende Diskriminierungsmuster verstärken.

analysis.notes: Das Werk entwirft KI-bezogene Kompetenzdimensionen (kognitiv, affektiv, handlungsbezogen) und eine eigene Übersicht der Besonderheiten algorithmen-basierter Diskriminierung (Tab. 1) für die Medienpädagogik. Nationality_Migration und Language_Culture stützen sich auf die berichtete Fokusgruppenstudie der Autorinnen mit Menschen mit Migrationsgeschichte (Klassifizierung nach kultureller Zugehörigkeit, Zuordnung zu einem Mehrheitssprachensystem, Autokorrektur ausländisch klingender Namen). Age stützt sich auf das ausgeführte Proxy-Beispiel im Bewerbungsverfahren. Geschlecht, Einkommen, Bildung und Religion stehen nur in Aufzählungen. Intersektionalität wird als Merkmal benannt, aber ohne Ergebnis oder Argument, das von einer Kombination abhängt, daher kein Intersectional. Indirect_Discrimination folgt aus der eigenen Übersicht (Proxy-Variablen) und dem Bewerbungsbeispiel, Exclusionary_Norms aus der Mehrheitssprach-Norm in der eigenen Studie. Die von Schober et al. berichteten beleidigenden Inhalte sind zitiert und nicht codiert. Maßnahmen sind vorgeschlagen, nämlich medienpädagogische Kompetenzförderung, Austauschforen, Meldesysteme, Beratungsstrukturen und regulatorische Anpassung des AGG. Kein theoretischer Rahmen für Bias, die Kompetenzdimensionen rahmen Kompetenz, nicht Bias. Studientyp Konzept, weil das Werk ein eigenes Modell der Kompetenzdimensionen (Abb. 1) und eine eigene Übersicht der Besonderheiten algorithmenbasierter Diskriminierung mit zugeordneten Kompetenzen (Tab. 1) entwirft und daraus Handlungsstrategien für die Medienpädagogik ableitet. Intersektionale Diskriminierung wird in einem Satz und einer Tabellenzeile benannt, ohne eigene Machtanalyse, daher Feministisch nein.

analysis.notes: General_Guidance strategy verbatim: 'Writing clear and detailed prompts to generate relevant and personalised content for youth.' and 'Training youth workers to divide information clearly and into defined blocks - prompts - will make it easier for AI systems to understand and process their input.' (4.2.4.4 National Focus Group - Portugal, Q4 and Q5). Prompting is a competence to be trained (Learning_Content) and a recommended practice. AN_Population: the codebook has no value for general youth work. evidence.snippet: Prompt engineering is the central skill for interacting with GenAI models and getting desired outputs for a given task (Wang, Shi, et al., 2023).

evidence.term: GenAI holds some promise for improving social work practice, primarily through i
evidence.snippet: GenAI holds some promise for improving social work practice, primarily through its ability to ease resource constraints for writing-oriented tasks

evidence.snippet: At the same time, social workers are now practicing in a world transformed by GenAI, and must be prepared to engage with these tools effectively and ethically.

analysis.notes: Vorschlag eines EPAS-Kompetenzindikators mit vier Fertigkeiten für das MSW-Curriculum. Prompting ist Lerninhalt (Fertigkeit 2) und empfohlene Praxis. Thought_Generation (Chain of Thought) und Role_Persona (Personas aus dem Prompt-Pattern-Katalog nach White et al.) sind als zu vermittelnde Techniken genannt. General_Guidance steht für das iterative Vorgehen 'The tasks of prompting and validating are often iterative'. Bias-Achsen und Schadensbeispiele (Bias gegenüber Frauen, People of Color, sexuell und geschlechtlich minorisierten Personen, CEO-Bilder, race-based medicine) sind zitierte Befunde anderer Arbeiten und nicht als eigene Analyse codiert, Geschlecht ist daher kein Gegenstand. Organisational_Process ist die vorgeschlagene Ausbildungsmaßnahme, Studierende sollen Ausgaben auf Bias prüfen und Minderung diskutieren. AN_Task folgt den im Werk beschriebenen Einsätzen, nämlich Behandlungspläne und Fallnotizen (Documentation_Recording), Materialien für Einzel- und Gruppensitzungen und Übersetzungen (Counselling_Client_Communication), Förderanträge und Fundraising (Administration), Schulungsmaterialien für die Fortbildung (Teaching_Further_Education) sowie die Zusammenfassung von Policy-Dokumenten und Entwürfe von Advocacy-Material auf Makroebene (Other_Task, Policy-Analyse und Advocacy). analysis.notes: Konzeptionelles Policy-Paper der Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung, das Feminist AI als Rahmen vorschlägt. Bias-Achse Geschlecht als eigenes Argument (männlich dominierte Verzerrungen, binäre Geschlechterkategorien schließen nicht-binäre Personen aus). Ethnizität, Klasse, Alter und weitere Kategorien stehen nur in der Bestimmung von Intersektionalität und in der Aufzählung der MIRA-Metriken, keine Passage macht ein Ergebnis von einer Achsenkombination abhängig, daher kein Intersectional. Schadensart Exclusionary_Norms aus dem eigenen Prüfkriterium zu binären Kategorien, die strukturelle Diskriminierung und das maskulinistische Intelligenzverständnis sind zitiert. Maßnahmen: Prüfung von Trainingsdaten auf Diversität und synthetische Trainingsdaten bei MIRA (Pre_Processing), diverse Teams, Stakeholder-Beteiligung, Feminist Design Tool, Gesetzgebung und Wartungszyklen (Organisational_Process). Demonstrated bezieht sich allein auf MIRA als umgesetztes und vorgestelltes Beispiel ohne berichtete Evaluation, die übrigen Maßnahmen bleiben Vorschläge. evidence.snippet: Social work curricula should be updated to include dedicated courses on AI and machine learning.

evidence.snippet: Algorithmic bias refers to the systematic and unfair discrimination against certain groups of individuals resulting from the design and implementation of algorithms.

evidence.snippet: Stakeholders in social work must advocate for diverse and inclusive datasets that accurately represent the populations they serve.

evidence.term: Social workers and organizations must be vigilant in assessing the fairness of p
evidence.snippet: Social workers and organizations must be vigilant in assessing the fairness of predictive models and ensuring that they promote equitable outcomes rather than exacerbating disparities (Barocas et al., 2019).

evidence.term: This paper explores how these technologies enhance case management, predictive a
evidence.snippet: This paper explores how these technologies enhance case management, predictive analytics, and resource allocation in critical areas such as child welfare, mental health, and substance abuse treatment.

evidence.term: Predictive analytics, powered by machine learning algorithms, can enhance decisi
evidence.snippet: Predictive analytics, powered by machine learning algorithms, can enhance decision-making by identifying at-risk populations and flagging cases that require immediate intervention, thus facilitating early support (Wang et al., 2022).

evidence.term: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) into s
evidence.snippet: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) into social work practice is transforming the landscape of service delivery and decision-making.

analysis.notes: Narrative review of AI and machine learning in social work: predictive risk analytics in child welfare, mental-health chatbots, NLP for case notes, automated case management, AI in social work education. AN_Bias_Axes Race_Ethnicity: the review develops the over-representation of families from certain ethnic backgrounds in child-abuse risk prediction as its own worked example (4.1) and returns to the Allegheny case (4.1.1). Socioeconomic (housing vouchers, Turner et al. 2020, absent from the reference list) and Language_Culture (English-only chatbots) appear only as single-sentence cited cases in 4.1.1, and gender only in the enumeration 'racial, gender, or socio-economic disparities', so they stay uncoded. AN_Harm_Types Indirect_Discrimination: the review's own argument in 4.1 places the disadvantage in risk scores learned from historical data that affect access to services and child welfare interventions, an allocation through biased data rather than the attribute itself; the work does not classify the discrimination. Mitigation Proposed: diverse and inclusive datasets (Pre_Processing); auditing, transparency, involvement of social workers and community members, AI training (Organisational_Process); none is assessed. AN_Task: predictive risk assessment (Case_Assessment_Decision_Support), mental-health chatbots (Counselling_Client_Communication), NLP summaries of case notes and automated documentation (Documentation_Recording), AI tools and AI-driven personalised learning in social work education and training (Teaching_Further_Education, Sections 5.3.3 and 6.1.1). Source quality: several in-text citations do not match the reference list, for example 'Baker et al., 2021' cited for NLP documentation while reference [3] is a review of AI in net-zero building design, 'Chukwunweike et al.' cited for predictive analytics in social work while reference [9] concerns loop execution in deep-learning systems, and 'Turner et al., 2020' absent from the list; this limits the evidential weight of the cited case studies without changing the publication type.

analysis.notes: Conceptual EPIC model derived from a literature review. Race_Ethnicity is coded because the work develops decolonisation of datasets and First Nations' and ethnic data sovereignty as its own strategy against structural bias. Gender, sexual orientation and the darker-skinned females result appear only as an enumeration and a cited finding (Buolamwini and Gebru) and are not coded. Exclusionary_Norms rests on the work's own argument that colonial knowledges dominate AI algorithms and on its limitation that the model assumes resources and access that marginalised groups may lack. Misdiagnosis, exclusion and discriminatory outcomes are cited from other work and not coded as further harm types. Mitigation stage: decolonisation of datasets is framed as a macro policy initiative for data sovereignty, control and community-based ownership, and representation of marginalised groups is framed as advocacy and participation; both are governance, so only Organisational_Process is coded and no data preparation step (Pre_Processing) is assigned. All measures are proposed. Theory reference: decolonisation of AI frames the treatment of structural bias. Bias is understood as unrepresentative historical data, without a determination of its own.

analysis.notes: Conceptual EPIC model derived from a literature review. Race_Ethnicity is coded because the work develops decolonisation of datasets and First Nations' and ethnic data sovereignty as its own strategy against structural bias. Gender, sexual orientation and the darker-skinned females result appear only as an enumeration and a cited finding (Buolamwini and Gebru) and are not coded. Exclusionary_Norms rests on the work's own argument that colonial knowledges dominate AI algorithms and on its limitation that the model assumes resources and access that marginalised groups may lack. Misdiagnosis, exclusion and discriminatory outcomes are cited from other work and not coded as further harm types. Mitigation stage: decolonisation of datasets is framed as a macro policy initiative for data sovereignty, control and community-based ownership, and representation of marginalised groups is framed as advocacy and participation; both are governance, so only Organisational_Process is coded and no data preparation step (Pre_Processing) is assigned. All measures are proposed. Theory reference: decolonisation of AI frames the treatment of structural bias. Bias is understood as unrepresentative historical data, without a determination of its own.

evidence.term: we can define gender bias as prejudicial attitudes or discriminatory actions bas
evidence.snippet: we can define gender bias as prejudicial attitudes or discriminatory actions based on an individual's gender identity.

evidence.term: With this understanding of gender, we can define gender bias as prejudicial atti
evidence.snippet: With this understanding of gender, we can define gender bias as prejudicial attitudes or discriminatory actions based on an individual's gender identity.

evidence.term: Inclusivity. This ensures the recognition and inclusion of multiple gender ident
evidence.snippet: Inclusivity. This ensures the recognition and inclusion of multiple gender identities, extending beyond the traditional binary to embrace transgender and nonbinary identities.

evidence.term: we develop effective debiasing techniques that incorporate counterfactual data a
evidence.snippet: we develop effective debiasing techniques that incorporate counterfactual data augmentation and specialized fine-tuning strategies to reduce gender bias in LLMs without compromising their overall performance.

evidence.term: we hope that our Gender CARE can represent a significant step towards achieving
evidence.snippet: we hope that our Gender CARE can represent a significant step towards achieving fairness and equity in LLMs.

evidence.term: At the lexical level, we utilize the Bias-Pair Ratio (BPR) to quantify the propo
evidence.snippet: At the lexical level, we utilize the Bias-Pair Ratio (BPR) to quantify the proportion of biased descriptors selected by the model.

evidence.term: Extensive experiments demonstrate a significant reduction in various gender bias
evidence.snippet: Extensive experiments demonstrate a significant reduction in various gender bias benchmarks, with reductions peaking at over 90% and averaging above 35% across 17 different LLMs.

evidence.term: Our approach addresses pertinent gaps in existing gender bias research across fo
evidence.snippet: Our approach addresses pertinent gaps in existing gender bias research across four interconnected facets: benchmark criteria, bias assessment, reduction, and quantification.

evidence.term: In this paper, we present Gender CARE , a comprehensive framework to assess and
evidence.snippet: In this paper, we present Gender CARE , a comprehensive framework to assess and reduce gender bias in LLMs.

evidence.term: Large language models (LLMs) have exhibited remarkable capabilities in natural l
evidence.snippet: Large language models (LLMs) have exhibited remarkable capabilities in natural language generation, but they have also been observed to magnify societal biases, particularly those related to gender.

evidence.term: Robustness. This pertains to the reliability and consistency of assessment outco
evidence.snippet: Robustness. This pertains to the reliability and consistency of assessment outcomes when evaluated across different prompt structures.

evidence.term: These pair sets serve as prompts for models, prompting them to select a descript
evidence.snippet: These pair sets serve as prompts for models, prompting them to select a descriptor and generate coherent text.

evidence.term: To evaluate the robustness of our GenderPair benchmark against variations in the
evidence.snippet: To evaluate the robustness of our GenderPair benchmark against variations in the prompt structure, we conduct tests on two representative LLMs, Alpaca and Vicuna, using three distinct prompt types

analysis.notes: Prompts des GenderPair-Benchmarks (Instruktion, Pair Set, Requirement) dienen als Messinstrument, Robustheit wird über drei Promptstrukturen geprüft, keine Prompting-Technik im Sinne des Codebuchs. Bias-Achse Geschlecht über drei Gruppen, transgender und nicht-binäre Identitäten bilden Gruppe 3. Das Werk führt alle drei Gruppen als Geschlechtsidentitäten und bestimmt Gender Bias über die Geschlechtsidentität, daher nur Gender und nicht zusätzlich Sexual_Orientation_Identity. Die Einbeziehung nicht-binärer Gruppen steht in AN_Gender_Understanding als Non_Binary_Inclusive. Race, Alter, Nationalität und Religion erscheinen nur im Ausblick (Abschnitt 6). Schadensarten: Stereotypisierung über Bias-Pair Ratio sowie Winoqueer und StereoSet, Toxizität als eigene Metrik je Gruppe. Regard-Differenzen messen Stimmung und begründen nach Regel 1.4.1 keine Disparate_Performance. Erasure nicht-binärer Personen wird nur aus Ovalle et al. zitiert. Maßnahmen: Counterfactual Data Augmentation zum Debiasing-Datensatz (Pre_Processing) und LoRA-Fine-Tuning (In_Training), in eigenen Experimenten evaluiert mit Bias-Reduktion auf GenderPair, Winoqueer, BOLD und StereoSet und Leistungsprüfung auf GLUE und MMLU. AN_Task None, allgemeiner LLM-Benchmark ohne Anwendungsaufgabe. Kein Theoriebezug, die Sex-Gender-Unterscheidung nach Tannenbaum et al. ist eine Begriffsbestimmung, NIST-Kriterien und die National Gender Equality Strategy inspirieren Benchmarkkriterien. Das Ethical Statement benennt westliche Gender-Konzeptionen als Grenze.

records.authors: Parrish, A.; Chen, A.; Nangia, N.; Padmakumar, V.; Bowman, S. R.

ai_verification.findings: The current productive record equals tests/review-cases/agent-runs/codebook-v141-includes-10-8-20261002/product-v0.5.json and the final coding of QY6P4RGQ in ai-agent-review.json (categories, decision, reason, evidence and analysis); the active annotation body matches; all 6 evidence terms and snippets resolve in generated/markdown_clean/Parrish_2022_BBQ_A_hand-built_bias_benchmark_for_question.md; the Work-Version identity equals the registry record index; the lifecycle state is ai-agent-reviewed without human verification or publication approval.

evidence.term: We introduce the Bias Benchmark for QA (BBQ), a dataset of question sets constru
evidence.snippet: We introduce the Bias Benchmark for QA (BBQ), a dataset of question sets constructed by the authors that highlight attested social biases against people belonging to protected classes along nine social dimensions relevant for U.S. English-speaking contexts.

evidence.term: we introduce a bias score to quantify the degree to which a model systematically
evidence.snippet: we introduce a bias score to quantify the degree to which a model systematically answers questions in a biased way

evidence.term: with this difference widening to over 5 points on examples targeting gender for
evidence.snippet: with this difference widening to over 5 points on examples targeting gender for most models tested

evidence.term: Large language models (LMs) learn social biases present in the world, and the in
evidence.snippet: Large language models (LMs) learn social biases present in the world, and the increased use of these systems across different contexts increases the cases where these biases can lead to harm.

evidence.term: We match each context with questions and answer options that test if a model sys
evidence.snippet: We match each context with questions and answer options that test if a model systematically relies on social biases.

evidence.term: UnifiedQA is trained on eight datasets and accepts multiple input string formats
evidence.snippet: UnifiedQA is trained on eight datasets and accepts multiple input string formats, so we include results for inputs with RACE-style (Lai et al., 2017) and ARC-style (Clark et al., 2018) formats.

analysis.notes: Benchmark mit Evaluation von UnifiedQA, RoBERTa und DeBERTaV3; Generative_KI ueber die Rahmung als Sprachmodelle und das generative UnifiedQA. Die handgeschriebenen Kontexte und Fragen sind Eingaben, die Modellverhalten als Bias-Test hervorrufen, mit kontrollierter Variation von Reihenfolge, Eingabeformat und UNKNOWN-Formulierungen (Research_Instrument), eine Prompting-Technik wird nicht benannt. Neun Achsen plus zwei intersektionale Kategorien (race by gender, race by SES); die intersektionalen Ergebnisse sind gemischt, die Kombination bestimmt aber Design und Auswertung. Keine Massnahme: 'This work does not directly contribute to debiasing'. Gender erscheint mit den Labels man/woman, girl/boy und Zensusnamen male/female, ohne Pruefung dieser Setzung. Theoriebezug: Begriff der representational harms nach Crawford (2017) rahmt die Bias-Bestimmung. Review: Der Theoriebezug Crawford dient zugleich als ausdrueckliche Bias-Definition, Grenzfall zwischen uebernommener Definition und rahmendem Konzept.

evidence.term: Artificial Intelligence (AI) should be created, critiqued, and reframed with an
evidence.snippet: Artificial Intelligence (AI) should be created, critiqued, and reframed with an awareness of power-valuing multiple perspectives and methodologies-in order to address the social inequalities, it reinforces.

evidence.term: Although it promises parity and efficiency, its computational processes mirror b
evidence.snippet: Although it promises parity and efficiency, its computational processes mirror biases of existing power even as oftenproprietary data practices and cultural perceptions of computational magic obscure those influences.

evidence.term: Thus, a combination of inclusive and reserved spaces best supports a variety of
evidence.snippet: Thus, a combination of inclusive and reserved spaces best supports a variety of communities and intersecting identities, in order to create safety and access, to share and prioritize resources and techniques as needed.

evidence.term: Because intersectional theory owes its roots to Black feminist thought, the stra
evidence.snippet: Because intersectional theory owes its roots to Black feminist thought, the strategies employed by women of color are at the core of an intersectional critical praxis.

evidence.term: reading AI through intersectional queer theory can push back on assumptions in A
evidence.snippet: reading AI through intersectional queer theory can push back on assumptions in AI about gender-and using queer strategies to disorient those categories can also push back on assumptions about technologies themselves.

evidence.term: An intersectional framework can be used to analyze the biases and problems built
evidence.snippet: An intersectional framework can be used to analyze the biases and problems built into existing Artificial Intelligence, as well as to uncover alternative ethics from its counterhistories.

analysis.notes: Theoretical essay applying intersectionality, Black feminist thought, queer theory and critical race theory to AI. Race is developed through the risk-assessment example the work frames as the New Jim Code and through Black feminist and POC community strategies; trans, bisexual and femme communities enter as categories of the argument (conceptual, not measured). The ProPublica and ImageNet harms are cited cases and stay uncoded; age, disability and ableism appear only in a cited quotation. The work's own argument is that normative algorithmic categorisation constrains identities that are not easily categorised (Exclusionary_Norms). Mitigation: intersectional strategies at data, design and implementation stages, community methodologies and the Data Nutrition Label as a data-collection example, proposed. Other_Task: artistic and tactical media practice with AI (the ladymouth chatbot, natural language processing in poetic practice). Gender definition coded Explicit through the adopted queer-theory determination that female is not a clearly defined natural category.

analysis.notes: Interpretative qualitative visual analysis of 180 Stable Diffusion XL images from 18 deliberately minimal prompts (poverty/wealth, criminal/law enforcement, immigrant/citizen, worker/executive, ideologies, everyday scenarios), followed by a micro, meso and macro intersectional analysis. Prompting is a research instrument; the recommendation that users be more conscious of the prompts they use is Recommended_Practice without a codable technique, so AN_Prompt_Techniques is None. Language_Culture covers cultural context and Global North hegemony in depictions of food and settings; Physical_Appearance covers body size and conventional attractiveness. Mitigation proposals: better curated training data (Pre_Processing), conscious prompting by users (Prompt_Practice), and algorithmic reparation, regulation, criminal culpability and diverse development teams (Organisational_Process); all proposed. Studientyp Empirisch rather than Experimentell because the prompt contrasts serve an interpretative analysis without a controlled comparison. The confederate flag is discussed as violent imagery, but Toxicity is not coded because the codebook ties it to language. AN_Task None because the work audits a general image generator without a professional application task. AI Agent Review: AN_Bias_Definition is Implicit_Only: the passages after Guillaumin and on intersectionality determine power systems and the interplay of oppressions, not bias or discrimination, and the work sets 'biases' in quotation marks without determining it. Fairness teilweise rests on the recommendations structured around algorithmic reparation as a foundation for building, evaluating and adjusting machine learning systems, with deliberate intervention and training data curation, a subordinate treatment of fair system design.

evidence.snippet: Across 3 preregistered experiments, members of stigmatized social groups (Black Americans, women) reported higher trustworthiness of LLMs after viewing unbiased interactions with ChatGPT compared to when viewing AI-generated prejudice (i.e., racial or gender d

analysis.notes: Drei präregistrierte Experimente zur Wirkung KI-generierter Vorurteile auf Vertrauenswürdigkeit und Nutzungsabsicht. Die ChatGPT-Antworten mit Gehaltsdisparitäten sind von den Autor:innen konstruierte Stimuli, das Werk misst nicht, ob LLMs solche Ausgaben erzeugen. AN_Harm_Types Indirect_Discrimination codiert die im Stimulus gezeigte Gehaltszuteilung, die über stereotyp Schwarze oder weibliche Vornamen (Jerome, Judi) variiert, nach der Regel zu namensbasierten Variationen. Grenzfall, weil der Mechanismus Gegenstand des eigenen Arguments ist, aber nicht am Modell gemessen wird. AN_Prompting_Role None, der gezeigte Prompt ist Teil des Stimulus und ruft kein Modellverhalten hervor. Minderung nur vorgeschlagen in 5.5, Nachjustieren der auf verzerrten Daten trainierten Algorithmen (In_Training) und Schulungen durch Lehrende oder Organisationen (Organisational_Process). Geschlecht wird binär verglichen, Personen anderen Geschlechts fallen aus den paarweisen Korrelationen heraus, der Satz zu Geschlechterrollen statt biologischem Geschlecht steht im Forschungsstand und trägt die Analyse nicht. Bias wird über Gehaltsdisparitäten, IAT und Modern Racism/Sexism Scale operationalisiert, ohne eigene Bestimmung. Intersektionalität und Alter werden in den Limitationen ausdrücklich als nicht untersucht benannt. Theoriebezug über UTAUT, erweitert um Rasse und Gender als Moderatoren, und das Vertrauensmodell nach Mayer et al. (1995).
