analysis.notes: Normatives Rahmenwerk aus Werten, Prinzipien und elf Politikfeldern für Mitgliedstaaten. Bias-Achsen: Geschlecht als eigenes Politikfeld (Policy Area 6, Ziffern 87 bis 93), Sprache und Kultur über die Wirkung von NLP-Anwendungen auf gefährdete Sprachen, Dialekte und tonale Variationen (Policy Area 7, Ziffer 95). Die langen Listen geschützter Merkmale sind Aufzählungen und bleiben uncodiert. Armutslücke (Ziffer 51), Stadt-Land-Gefälle (Ziffern 28, 67) und LMICs behandeln Zugangsungleichheit und digitale Spaltung, nicht Bias eines Systems entlang einer Achse, daher weder Socioeconomic noch Other_Axis. Schadensarten: Stereotypisierung aus dem eigenen Argument zur Reproduktion von Bias und Stereotypen (Ziffern 2(c), 66 und 90), Erasure aus dem Verschwinden gefährdeter Sprachen und Dialekte durch NLP-Anwendungen (Ziffer 95). Diskriminierende algorithmische Entscheidungen (Ziffer 29) werden ohne Zuteilungsfall und ohne Einordnung als unmittelbar oder mittelbar genannt und daher nicht codiert. Maßnahmen: Datenvorbereitung (diverse Trainingsdaten, Gold-Standard-Datensätze, nach Geschlecht disaggregierte Annotation, Ziffern 67 und 76) und Organisation (Ethical Impact Assessment mit Gender-Perspektive, AI Ethics Officers, Aufsicht, Audit, Zertifizierung, diverse Teams), durchgehend als Empfehlung, daher Proposed. AN_Task None: das Instrument regelt die Governance von KI über alle Sektoren und nennt Einsatzfelder wie Gesundheit oder Kulturerbe nur allgemein, ohne eine bestimmte berufliche Aufgabe. Geschlecht erscheint als Mädchen und Frauen gegenüber Männern ohne eigene Bestimmung, strukturelle Gender-Gaps (Ziffer 89) werden benannt, eine ausdrückliche Aussage zu Geschlecht als sozialer Konstruktion fehlt. Bias-Verständnis implizit über Nicht-Diskriminierung im Menschenrechtsrahmen, Ziffer 28 bestimmt Fairness als inklusiven Zugang zu den Vorteilen von KI. Kein Theoriebezug, das Völkerrecht ist ein rechtlich-normativer Bezug. Soziale_Arbeit nein, welfare erscheint nur in einer Aufzählung menschenrechtssensibler Einsatzbereiche (Ziffer 62).

evidence.snippet: Interestingly, CoT prompting reduces this unconscious social bias in LLMs and encourages fair predictions.

evidence.snippet: In this study, we examine the impact of LLMs' step-by-step predictions on gender bias in unscalable tasks.

analysis.notes: Own benchmark MGBR on 23 LLMs. Techniques tested: Zero-shot+CoT ('Let's think step by step.'), Few-shot with pro-stereotypical demonstrations (ICL), Debiasing Prompt as General_Guidance with the strategy 'Please ensure that your answer is unbiased and does not rely on stereotypes.' evidence.snippet: The EiCAT score ranges from 0 to 1 and quantitatively evaluates fairness and effectiveness in local contexts of LLMs, with higher scores indicating better performance and less bias.

evidence.snippet: we use prompt template P 1 to extract its definition D 1 from an LLM and compare it with the official definition D 2

analysis.notes: Bias measurement framework (LIBRA, EiCAT metric) for local cultural contexts, applied to New Zealand, a youth corpus and Malaysian English. Language_Culture is the axis the work analyses (local culture, Te Reo Maori and Malay words). The dataset spans eight target groups (age, gender, race/ethnicity, sexual orientation, physical appearance, disability, nationality, religion), but results are reported only in aggregate per model and context, so these axes are not coded and gender is not an object of the analysis. Stereotyping: the measured preference for stereotyped over anti-stereotyped sentences. Disparate_Performance: models fail to understand local non-English words, a quality difference between language varieties. Prompting appears only as a template for definition extraction. Bias is determined explicitly through the adopted definition of [14] and the JSD-based measure. No mitigation is applied or specified: the concluding sentence on 'incorporating localized and contextually rich data in evaluating and improving LLM fairness' and the remark on continuous improvements in model training are generic and name no identifiable intervention, so no stage is coded.

evidence.term: Participatory AI projects should begin with AI literacy efforts, as participants
evidence.snippet: Participatory AI projects should begin with AI literacy efforts, as participants need a foundational understanding of what AI is, and what it is not, in order to meaningfully engage in discussions about how such systems may affect their lives [99].

evidence.snippet: we dare argue that AI experts do have the duty to invest in educating themselves to the level that they can collaborate within interdisciplinary teams and communities that bring their expertise on power and social context.

evidence.term: Yet in AI research, intersectionality is often reduced to a narrow technical len

evidence.snippet: We call on AI experts to meet this challenge through interdisciplinary collaboration with diverse communities.

evidence.term: This interpretation of intersectional subgroup fairness is criticized for being
evidence.snippet: This interpretation of intersectional subgroup fairness is criticized for being narrow and primarily technical [59, 73] as it mainly leads to algorithmic solutions, such as defining and optimizing for multidimensional fairness metrics.

evidence.term: Intersectionality, rooted in Black Feminist movements, is increasingly used to a
evidence.snippet: Intersectionality, rooted in Black Feminist movements, is increasingly used to address the interconnected nature of discrimination such as racism, ableism, and sexism.

evidence.term: Yet intersectionality, grounded in Black Feminist thought, offers a much broader
evidence.snippet: Yet intersectionality, grounded in Black Feminist thought, offers a much broader framework that can support AI experts in addressing the structural dimensions of unfairness through a social justice lens.

evidence.term: On top of that, would a racially profiled Black woman care about more equal erro
evidence.snippet: On top of that, would a racially profiled Black woman care about more equal errors if she has limited opportunity to contest the errors that occur?

evidence.term: An intersectional question would be: if we have for example women or queer repre
evidence.snippet: An intersectional question would be: if we have for example women or queer representation in the team or the advisory panel, do we have only the most privileged subgroup of the marginalized group?

evidence.term: Since the primary focus of AI fairness papers centres around the development and
evidence.snippet: Since the primary focus of AI fairness papers centres around the development and research of machine learning-based AI applications, we adopt this same scope for our study.

evidence.term: The Dutch childcare benefits scandal, exposed in 2019, starkly illustrates how b
evidence.snippet: The Dutch childcare benefits scandal, exposed in 2019, starkly illustrates how biased use of algorithmic systems harms marginalized groups.

evidence.term: A similar case emerged in France, where an automated fraud detection system used
evidence.snippet: A similar case emerged in France, where an automated fraud detection system used in welfare allocation disproportionately flagged individuals from low-income and immigrant backgrounds, leading to exclusion from vital benefits [4, 67, 82, 83].

analysis.notes: Thematic analysis of 63 FAccT and AIES papers, evaluated in a workshop with AI experts. Bias axes follow the work's own worked example in the introduction (Black women and image recognition, racially profiled Black woman); the welfare cases (dual nationality, low-income and immigrant backgrounds) are cited cases and stay uncoded as axes. Harm types: the harms named (welfare fraud scandals, Gender Shades error disparities, COMPAS) are cited cases that the work's own argument does not establish, and the five themes structure recommendations, not harm types, so None. Mitigation: all five themes are organisational (interdisciplinary teams, positionality statements, community co-ownership, power analysis, documentation of data and metrics). The workshop gauged perceived actionability of intermediate recommendation versions, not the effect of an applied mitigation, so the status stays Proposed. Gender is treated only within the intersectional frame and is not defined; race, not gender, is explicitly called a social construct, so Social_Construct is not coded. AN_Task None because the work addresses AI development practice, not AI use for a professional task.

evidence.snippet: we probed the presence of stereotypes within two contemporary LLMs, GPT-3 (Brown et al., 2020) and ChatGPT.

evidence.term: The design of our prompts, which are used to retrieve stereotypes from ChatGPT,
evidence.snippet: The design of our prompts, which are used to retrieve stereotypes from ChatGPT, encompasses three key components: the problem statement, regulation, and disclaimer.

analysis.notes: Dataset and stereotype examination of GPT-3 and ChatGPT across intersectional groups built from six demographic categories. Other_Axis: political leaning (conservative and progressive) is one of the six categories from which the analysed groups are constructed and enters the measured results, for example 'conservative Muslim men'; political opinion is a recognised ground of discrimination, so it is coded as a further social axis. Role_Persona: simulated life-story roles the models answer as; Self_Criticism: ChatGPT filters stereotypes in its own generated responses. Gender is introduced in section 2.1 as men and women, but Table 1 and Tables C1 and C2 include non-binary groups as categories of the analysis, so Non_Binary_Inclusive follows the analysis (internal inconsistency of the source). Bias is determined explicitly as consistent answers in one category across trials (Stereotype Degree). Mitigation: the limitations recommend that future work 'cautiously regulate the output through effective prompting' to counter biases that the LLM's viewpoints introduce into the dataset, a proposed prompt-level measure; the general call for future de-biasing names no stage. Intersectionality is used as a combination of demographic attributes without a named theory, so no theory reference is coded.

evidence.snippet: In 2003, McPhail devised the Feminist Policy Analysis Framework, a qualitative action-oriented model that utilizes 13 categories to examine how public policy reifies gendered systems of oppression.

evidence.term: This working paper utilizes a feminist policy analysis framework centred around
evidence.snippet: This working paper utilizes a feminist policy analysis framework centred around five thematic areas - intersectionality, context, neutrality, control and power - to analyze global initiatives for AI safety governance.

evidence.term: The feminist AI policy framework was used to examine seven international initiat
evidence.snippet: The feminist AI policy framework was used to examine seven international initiatives regarding AI safety governance.

analysis.notes: Feministische Policy-Analyse von sieben internationalen AI-Safety-Initiativen mit einem eigenen Bewertungsraster (vier Ziele mit je drei Fragen, Punktwerte je Initiative). Die Achsen stammen aus dem eigenen Argument gegen eine vermeintlich universelle Bedrohung im Befund zu combat neutrality, nämlich eine einkommensschwache Familie, die durch einen diskriminierenden Algorithmus Sozialleistungen verliert (Socioeconomic), sowie ländliche und indigene Gemeinschaften ohne Wasserzugang durch Rechenzentren (Race_Ethnicity für indigen, Other_Axis für den Wohnort im ländlichen Raum). Geschlecht steht nur in Aufzählungen, im Intersektionalitätsbegriff und im zitierten UN-Text, daher keine Gender-Achse. Intersektionalität ist Rahmen und Bewertungsziel, ein Ergebnis, das von einer Achsenkombination abhängt, fehlt, daher weder Intersectional in AN_Bias_Axes noch in AN_Gender_Understanding. Exclusionary_Norms folgt aus dem eigenen Befund, dass die Initiativen eine universelle, neutrale Sicht auf Risiko setzen und Erfahrungen marginalisierter Gruppen auslassen. Das Wohlfahrtsbeispiel ist eine allokative Benachteiligung, die das Werk weder als unmittelbare noch als mittelbare Diskriminierung einordnet, und bleibt ohne Diskriminierungscode. Vorgeschlagene Maßnahmen sind Audits mit dem Framework, Rechenschaftspflicht von Unternehmen, Beteiligung marginalisierter Gruppen, Bürger:innenjurys und digitale Literacy (Organisational_Process). Geschlecht wird nicht bestimmt, und das Werk sagt nicht selbst, dass Geschlecht sozial hergestellt oder eine Machtstruktur ist. Die Wendung 'gendered systems of oppression' beschreibt den Zweck des übernommenen Rahmens nach McPhail, daher nach der Schwelle von 1.4.1 kein Social_Construct, sondern Unclear mit Absent. Bias wird als Reproduktion sozialer Ungleichheit und Machtverhältnisse gerahmt, aber nicht bestimmt, die Crenshaw-Passage bestimmt Intersektionalität und nicht Bias. Theorien sind Intersektionalität nach Crenshaw, das Feminist Policy Analysis Framework nach McPhail und Data Feminism nach D'Ignazio und Klein.

analysis.notes: Systematic review of nine implementation studies of predictive risk tools in child welfare, structured by CFIR and the ethical evaluation frameworks of Russell (2015) and Drake et al. (2020). AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated is a synthesised evaluation, not the review's own experiment: the review reports that the post-processing fairness correction of Purdy and Glass (2023), group-specific risk thresholds, reduced false positive and false negative error rates among four subgroups; it also reports the racial equity report of Putnam-Hornstein et al. (2022) finding comparable accuracy across racial and ethnic groups. Other mitigation stages remain description or recommendation: exclusion of bias-prone variables after community consultation and feature selection (Pre_Processing), stakeholder consensus, training against automation bias and external ethics reviews (Organisational_Process). Race_Ethnicity is the axis of the synthesised subgroup analyses, thresholds and equity reports; gender is mentioned once as a subgroup dimension of accuracy checks and socioeconomic status only in a cited discussion sentence, so both stay uncoded. Harm types follow the review's own synthesis: subgroup error rates and equity in subgroups as Disparate_Performance, historical bias in administrative records and racial disparities in screening outcomes as Indirect_Discrimination. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit rests on the adopted equity criterion of Russell (2015), 'equity evaluates whether predictions function consistently across subgroups'. AN_Theory_Reference No (resolved by the AI Agent Review): Russell (2015) and Drake et al. (2020) are evaluation criteria and a practical framework that the review uses as an assessment checklist, and CFIR is an implementation framework; the review itself names the limited use of theoretical frameworks as a gap and mentions feminist and other critical theories only as a future-research suggestion. Boundary case flagged for domain experts.

analysis.notes: Experiment with Stable Diffusion, DALL-E 3 (via ChatGPT-4) and Adobe Firefly on 16 base prompts with demographic modifiers and modifier order. General_Guidance strategy verbatim: 'combining base prompts with modifiers and their sequencing', 'Base Prompt + Modifier' versus 'Modifier + Base'. Prompts are the measurement instrument and prompt modification is itself analysed and found insufficient as bias control. Bias axes as named by the work: gender, race, geography (coded Nationality_Migration, e.g. Korean soldier, US politician, person in Africa) and region/culture (coded Language_Culture, e.g. Lunar New Year); religion appears only as category label for pastor and monk prompts that are evaluated for gender and race, so Religion is not coded. Combined prompts such as 'Monk who is black' are not analysed for interaction effects, so Intersectional is not coded. Mitigation evaluated with a mixed result (modifiers shift distributions but not consistently, order matters). Gender is counted male/female in the result tables. AI Agent Review: Religion stays uncoded because pastor and monk prompts are evaluated for gender and race only and no output is compared across religious groups. The East Asian default for 'Asian' is coded as Misrepresentation, an unrepresentative depiction generalised to the group Asian, not as Erasure.

analysis.notes: German conference handout on power and digitalisation in social work with case vignettes and reflection questions. Other_Axis: place of residence (Stadtteil), used as worked example of proxy discrimination. Axes coded from the work's own case examples (child-welfare algorithm and migration background, social-assistance AI and Black and migrant applicants, debt scoring and low-income districts, job-centre scoring by age, school education and district); Frauen, disability and language appear only in enumerations of affected groups and are not coded. Harm: Direct_Discrimination where the score uses origin itself (scoring features 'Einkommen, Alter, Herkunft'), Indirect_Discrimination via district as proxy, Exclusionary_Norms via digital-only access to benefits. Mitigation proposed at organisational and political level: participation of professionals and clients, human control, transparency and right to object, reflection methods ('Macht-Check', Ethik-Cafés), regulation and ban of discriminatory systems. AI tasks: risk assessment and scoring (case assessment), AI chat tool helping clients with applications (client communication), ChatGPT-connected avatar Konrad for workshops and social-media teaching. Gender is no object of the work. Bias is described as prejudice carried from old data into algorithms without a definition.

records.authors: Voutyrakou, D. A.; Skordoulis, C.

evidence.term: Across all four experiments, the AI tools consistently reflected underlying stru
evidence.snippet: Across all four experiments, the AI tools consistently reflected underlying structural gender biases.

evidence.term: These recommendations suggest that when explicitly prompted, AI tools are capabl
evidence.snippet: These recommendations suggest that when explicitly prompted, AI tools are capable of generating thoughtful and inclusive designs that better serve non-binary individuals and other gender-diverse users.

evidence.term: The aim was to evaluate the inclusivity
evidence.snippet: The aim was to evaluate the inclusivity

evidence.term: In addition, for the first and fourth prompts, we included variations that refer
evidence.snippet: In addition, for the first and fourth prompts, we included variations that referenced non-binary individuals.

evidence.term: Our findings offer insights into the limitations of current AI tools as policy a
evidence.snippet: Our findings offer insights into the limitations of current AI tools as policy advisors and contribute to ongoing discussions on algorithmic fairness, implicit gender bias, and the need for gender-aware AI governance.

evidence.term: This underscores a broader concern in algorithmic governance: as Mehrabi et al.
evidence.snippet: This underscores a broader concern in algorithmic governance: as Mehrabi et al. emphasize [52], fairness interventions must align with real-world harm mitigation and not merely with metric optimization.

evidence.term: This reveals that the supposed neutrality of AI tools actually reproduces an and
evidence.snippet: This reveals that the supposed neutrality of AI tools actually reproduces an androcentric norm, which in this case excludes bodies and needs not aligned with the gendered definition of the 'typical worker'.

evidence.term: Feminist theory has pointed out how seemingly neutral technical standards, like
evidence.snippet: Feminist theory has pointed out how seemingly neutral technical standards, like office temperature, can produce bodily inequalities and disproportionately affect women [45].

evidence.term: This study examines whether AI systems inherently consider gender in policy prop
evidence.snippet: This study examines whether AI systems inherently consider gender in policy proposals, both when gender is explicitly mentioned in prompts and when it is not.

evidence.term: We tested these experiments in two different AI tools, namely ChatGPT (GPT-4) an
evidence.snippet: We tested these experiments in two different AI tools, namely ChatGPT (GPT-4) and Microsoft Copilot.

evidence.term: Each scenario includes a gender-neutral prompt, a male-specific version, and a f
evidence.snippet: Each scenario includes a gender-neutral prompt, a male-specific version, and a female-specific version and a non-binary-specific version.

evidence.term: This contrast suggests that ChatGPT adapts its responses to perceived gender-bas
evidence.snippet: This contrast suggests that ChatGPT adapts its responses to perceived gender-based risks only when explicitly mentioned, reinforcing the importance of demographic framing in prompt design.

evidence.term: Crucially, gender-specific considerations are largely omitted unless explicitly
evidence.snippet: Crucially, gender-specific considerations are largely omitted unless explicitly prompted, underscoring the importance of precise, inclusive language in AI-assisted design and policy applications.

analysis.notes: Prompt experiment with ChatGPT (GPT-4) and Microsoft Copilot on four policy scenarios (restrooms, snow removal, office temperature, business-trip expenses), each prompt variant submitted 50 times in neutral, male, female and partly non-binary or new-mother versions; themes retained at a 70 percent threshold. Prompting is the research instrument and the object of the central finding. General_Guidance, verbatim strategy: 'the importance of precise, inclusive language in AI-assisted design and policy applications', i.e. naming the gendered target group explicitly in the prompt; the work adds that equity principles must be embedded 'not just in prompts'. Other_Task: drafting workplace and municipal policy recommendations, outside social work. Bias_Axes: gender is varied in every scenario, and non-binary employees are an analysed group of their own (restroom and business-trip prompts), coded as Sexual_Orientation_Identity under the codebook label for gender identity; race, class and ability appear only as intersecting factors in the discussion, so Intersectional is not coded. Harm types from the work's own results: male default (Exclusionary_Norms), omission of women's and non-binary needs in unspecified prompts (Erasure), baby-changing facilities only in women's restrooms read as care stereotype (Stereotyping). Mitigation only proposed: curated gender-balanced and intersectional datasets (Pre_Processing), fine-tuning (In_Training), equity principles in prompts (Prompt_Practice), audits, Human-in-the-Loop oversight and multidisciplinary teams (Organisational_Process). Social_Construct rests on the applied statement after Connell that gender relations are institutionally embedded in everyday practices; the work also uses metabolic differences between women and men as a factual premise. Theory frame: Tronto's ethics of care, Young's justice as inclusion, capabilities approach, Connell, Grosz, feminist spatial planning, design justice.

evidence.snippet: Our framework continuously collects annotations from a diverse pool of volunteer participants on LabintheWild, and statistically quantifies alignment with dataset labels and model predictions.

evidence.snippet: Our results indicate the need for more inclusive models and datasets, paving the way for NLP research that benefits all people.

evidence.snippet: Additionally, certain groups, such as nonbinary people and non-native English speakers, are further marginalized by datasets and models as they rank least in alignment across all tasks.

evidence.term: We examine datasets and supervised models related to these tasks as well as gene
evidence.snippet: We examine datasets and supervised models related to these tasks as well as generalpurpose large language models (i.e., GPT-4).

evidence.term: We introduce NLPositionality , a framework for characterizing design biases and
evidence.snippet: We introduce NLPositionality , a framework for characterizing design biases and quantifying the positionality of NLP datasets and models.

evidence.term: To evaluate GPT-4, we use the prompt used by Rae et al. (2021):
evidence.snippet: To evaluate GPT-4, we use the prompt used by Rae et al. (2021):

analysis.notes: Annotation study: re-annotation of Social Chemistry and Dynahate by LabintheWild volunteers, correlated with dataset labels and model predictions (Delphi, GPT-4, Perspective API, Rewire API, ToxiGen RoBERTa). Axes from the compared demographics in Table 2: gender including non-binary, ethnicity, age, education level (Socioeconomic), native language and cultural spheres (Language_Culture), country lived longest and country of residence (Nationality_Migration; the work names the variable country and groups it into cultural spheres, so both are coded), religion. Intersectional not coded, since the limitations state that Pearson's r does not consider interaction effects. GPT-4 is queried zero-shot with a fixed template, no technique family. Recommendations: documenting design choices and positionality, participatory and value-sensitive design, diverse teams (Organisational_Process); diverse annotators and disaggregated labels (Pre_Processing); modelling techniques that handle annotator disagreement instead of one label (In_Training); all Proposed. AN_Task None: NLP benchmark tasks without a professional task. The sentence that gender is culturally ascribed belongs to the background on positionality; the analysis treats gender as self-reported categories, so Social_Construct is not coded and the definition stays Implicit_Only.

analysis.notes: Prompt tuning (trainable soft prompt embeddings concatenated to the input of frozen BERT and RoBERTa) as a debiasing method, trained on 159 gender-profession templates with a KL-divergence loss towards the average distribution across groups, evaluated on SEAT and StereoSet with language-modelling score and pseudo-perplexity against CDA, Dropout, INLP, SentenceDebias and Self-Debias. Generative_KI is teilweise: the work frames its object as large language models and language generation, but its method and experiments concern encoder-only masked language models. Prompting is the proposed mitigation practice; soft prompt tuning belongs to none of the technique families, and in-context learning appears only as motivation, so AN_Prompt_Techniques = None. Mitigation stage: the work places its intervention at inference ('additional information at inference') with model weights frozen, coded Intra_Processing; the trained parameters are prompt embeddings, not the model, so In_Training is not coded. The intervention changes the model input, coded Prompt_Practice. Evaluated with mixed results (on par with the state of the art, second to INLP on BERT). Axes: gender is the target; race and religion are measured as side effects on StereoSet. Harm type: stereotyping measured by the StereoSet stereotype score; the Gallegos harm list in the introduction is background and not coded. Gender is operationalised as he/she and male/female name pairs without a definition. Bias is determined technically by the stereotype score near 50 percent and by the reference distribution averaged across groups. AN_Task None: benchmark study without an application task.

evidence.snippet: Moving away from LLMs, we find Neural Machine Translation models

evidence.snippet: Fortunately, after identifying our successful prompt, we can confidently affirm that leveraging prompting can indeed serve as an effective method to mitigate gender bias in an instructed LLM

analysis.notes: Benchmark von drei Basis-LLMs gegen vier NMT-Systeme auf WinoMT, Gold BUG, MuST-SHE und FLoRes-200 (En nach Ca und Es), danach Versuch-und-Irrtum-Suche nach einem Prompt für Llama-2-7B-chat. AN_Prompting_Role Research_Instrument über die 5-Shot-Prompts im Benchmark, Recommended_Practice über die Schlussfolgerung, Prompting sei eine wirksame Minderungsmethode. AN_Prompt_Techniques ICL (Few-Shot), Thought_Generation (Chain-of-Thought einschließlich der kurzen schematischen Variante), General_Guidance für das Context-Supplying, konkret die Systemanweisung, beim Übersetzen Gender Bias zu mindern und ohne Genderhinweis mit der Anweisung ensure fair gender treatment in the output zufällige Genusformen zu wählen. Dieser Prompt brachte laut Diskussion keine Verbesserung. AN_Harm_Types Stereotyping über die Korrelation mit pro- und antistereotypen Sets, Exclusionary_Norms über überwiegend männliche Formen ohne Genderhinweis, Disparate_Performance über die Differenz der Erkennungsgüte männlicher und weiblicher Terme (Delta G). AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated, der Prompt mit erfundenen antistereotypen Winograd-Beispielen und kurzer Chain-of-Thought senkt den Bias auf den Gender-Testsets bei leichtem Verlust an Übersetzungsqualität. AN_Task Other_Task, maschinelle Übersetzung als Anwendungsaufgabe außerhalb der Sozialen Arbeit. Die einmalige Erwähnung repräsentationaler und allokativer Schäden in der Einleitung rahmt die Analyse nicht, daher AN_Theory_Reference No. Geschlecht nur binär, im Ethical Statement als Grenze benannt.

evidence.term: To address this gap, we implemented a critical co-discovery approach within an o

evidence.snippet: One educator noted that a student from Kenya appeared in similar clothing across various countries, reflecting a lack of cultural specificity and diversity in the AI's outputs.

evidence.snippet: One notable bias uncovered by some participants was gender bias. For example, one participant noted, when generating images of CEOs, the AI predominantly produced images of men.

evidence.snippet: Teacher education increasingly requires educators to engage with generative AI technologies, yet critical and reflective engagement opportunities remain scarce.

evidence.term: They then generate images based on prompts like 'a person,' 'a woman,' 'a house,
evidence.snippet: They then generate images based on prompts like 'a person,' 'a woman,' 'a house,' 'a street,' and 'a plate of food,' incorporating variations with cultural or geographical descriptors.

analysis.notes: Illustrative case study with artifact analysis of nine educators in an online AI in Education course. Prompts in the activity Experimenting With Algorithmic Bias elicit image-generator output as a bias probe (Research_Instrument), no named technique. Bias axes from the findings: gender (CEO images) and cultural bias, which the work names cultural (country depictions), coded as Language_Culture. Harm types from participant artifacts: stereotypes, misleading generalised depictions of countries and cultures, the male default for CEO images. Mitigation: the critical co-discovery course as training of educators (Organisational_Process); the work presents an illustrative case of an implemented course and reports educators' engagement, not a completed assessment of a bias outcome, hence Demonstrated. Gender appears only as men and women. Theory reference: the framing of generative AI as a socio-technical system embedded in power structures that perpetuates inequalities and biases frames the bias activity and its discussion; constructivism, speculative design and discursive closure frame the pedagogy.

analysis.notes: Multilingual and multicultural prompting: several prompt variants with language and cultural cues (e.g. 'You are a Chinese-speaking assistant', persona with name, birthplace, favourite food), responses combined by concatenation (Ensembling) and compared against high temperature, requesting diversity, random personas and step-by-step recall on GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA 70B and 8B. Evaluated: multilingual prompting yields the highest normalized entropy in most comparisons and lowers hallucination of culture-specific names in a human annotation study (own experiment). Harm types from the own experiment: American default in named artists (Exclusionary_Norms) and overlooking underrepresented cultural backgrounds (Erasure). analysis.notes: Edited volume (introduction, sixteen chapters, outlook) coded as one Work; codes collect what individual chapters carry as their own argument or result. Studientyp Theoretisch after the predominantly conceptual chapters; Plafky et al. report own usability tests and a focus group on an LLM case-note prototype, Holz et al. demonstrate classical NLP on a synthetic case, Schlomann draws on the KI-Alter field study. General_Guidance strategy: Plafky et al. instruct a local Mistral 7B with a fixed case-note structure (Wer, Wann, Wo, Grund, Ablauf, Diskussionsinhalte, Vereinbarungen, fachliche Interpretation, Entscheidung, naechster Termin; Tabelle 1), and testers ask for selectable templates per note type; Botzum et al. propose mandatory documentation of the prompts students used. AN_Prompting_Role: Learning_Content from Beranek (prompting as communicative competence), Recommended_Practice from Plafky et al. and Botzum et al., Object_of_Critique from Pelzl's analysis of prompting attacks as a manipulation practice. AN_Bias_Axes: Gender (Beranek's own example list, Schlomann's gendered digital divide), Race_Ethnicity (Steiner on the AFST and ethnically marginalised children), Disability (Steiner's chapter makes AI-related exclusion of disabled people its object and demands models that do not reinforce exclusion 'vor allem im Bereich Behinderung'), Age (Schlomann, age discrimination as own argument), Socioeconomic (editors' Allegheny poverty example, Schlomann on education), Language_Culture (Plafky et al., own observation that Swiss German dialect recognition depends on proximity to Standard German), Nationality_Migration (editors' bias-audit example and the Dutch child-benefit case). Sexual orientation appears only in enumerations. Intersectional not coded: the BIPoC-women facial-recognition result is cited from Buolamwini/Gebru without an own argument that depends on the combination. AN_Harm_Types: Exclusionary_Norms (editors: addressees deviate from the norm dominating internet training data), Erasure (Steiner: data selection and weighting under-represent marginalised discourses and groups; Tappe: AI-generated visual narratives decide which cultural references remain invisible), Disparate_Performance (own observation on dialect recognition, a quality difference between language varieties). Amazon hiring, Dutch child benefit, Allegheny risk scores, UNESCO images and Gender Shades are cited cases and stay uncoded under rule 1.4.1. AN_Mitigation_Status Proposed: training-data analysis, exclusion or synthetic data (Pre_Processing) and bias audit, diverse developer teams, ethics boards, human-in-the-loop and staff training (Organisational_Process) are recommended; the AFST evaluation reported by Steiner concerns a decision-support tool's side effect on ethnic disparities, not a tested bias mitigation. AN_Gender_Definition Absent and AN_Gender_Understanding Unclear: gender appears only in short discrimination examples, the cited gender gap of older women and men, and enumerations that also name LGBTQIA+ and queer people; no chapter determines gender, and these signals do not settle a binary or any other understanding. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit (Loehe; Dummann footnote 6; also Rottkemper). AN_Theory_Reference: Steiner frames under-representation and exclusion through a critical conception of inclusion and exclusion (Luhmann, Stichweh) with critical theory and Rojas' radical inclusion concept; Staub-Bernasconi, Media Equation and CASA frame ethics or communication, not gender or bias. Feministisch nein: no feminist theory or method and no structural gender critique.

analysis.notes: Edited volume (introduction, sixteen chapters, outlook) coded as one Work; codes collect what individual chapters carry as their own argument or result. Studientyp Theoretisch after the predominantly conceptual chapters; Plafky et al. report own usability tests and a focus group on an LLM case-note prototype, Holz et al. demonstrate classical NLP on a synthetic case, Schlomann draws on the KI-Alter field study. General_Guidance strategy: Plafky et al. instruct a local Mistral 7B with a fixed case-note structure (Wer, Wann, Wo, Grund, Ablauf, Diskussionsinhalte, Vereinbarungen, fachliche Interpretation, Entscheidung, naechster Termin; Tabelle 1), and testers ask for selectable templates per note type; Botzum et al. propose mandatory documentation of the prompts students used. AN_Prompting_Role: Learning_Content from Beranek (prompting as communicative competence), Recommended_Practice from Plafky et al. and Botzum et al., Object_of_Critique from Pelzl's analysis of prompting attacks as a manipulation practice. AN_Bias_Axes: Gender (Beranek's own example list, Schlomann's gendered digital divide), Race_Ethnicity (Steiner on the AFST and ethnically marginalised children), Disability (Steiner's chapter makes AI-related exclusion of disabled people its object and demands models that do not reinforce exclusion 'vor allem im Bereich Behinderung'), Age (Schlomann, age discrimination as own argument), Socioeconomic (editors' Allegheny poverty example, Schlomann on education), Language_Culture (Plafky et al., own observation that Swiss German dialect recognition depends on proximity to Standard German), Nationality_Migration (editors' bias-audit example and the Dutch child-benefit case). Sexual orientation appears only in enumerations. Intersectional not coded: the BIPoC-women facial-recognition result is cited from Buolamwini/Gebru without an own argument that depends on the combination. AN_Harm_Types: Exclusionary_Norms (editors: addressees deviate from the norm dominating internet training data), Erasure (Steiner: data selection and weighting under-represent marginalised discourses and groups; Tappe: AI-generated visual narratives decide which cultural references remain invisible), Disparate_Performance (own observation on dialect recognition, a quality difference between language varieties). Amazon hiring, Dutch child benefit, Allegheny risk scores, UNESCO images and Gender Shades are cited cases and stay uncoded under rule 1.4.1. AN_Mitigation_Status Proposed: training-data analysis, exclusion or synthetic data (Pre_Processing) and bias audit, diverse developer teams, ethics boards, human-in-the-loop and staff training (Organisational_Process) are recommended; the AFST evaluation reported by Steiner concerns a decision-support tool's side effect on ethnic disparities, not a tested bias mitigation. AN_Gender_Definition Absent and AN_Gender_Understanding Unclear: gender appears only in short discrimination examples, the cited gender gap of older women and men, and enumerations that also name LGBTQIA+ and queer people; no chapter determines gender, and these signals do not settle a binary or any other understanding. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit (Loehe; Dummann footnote 6; also Rottkemper). AN_Theory_Reference: Steiner frames under-representation and exclusion through a critical conception of inclusion and exclusion (Luhmann, Stichweh) with critical theory and Rojas' radical inclusion concept; Staub-Bernasconi, Media Equation and CASA frame ethics or communication, not gender or bias. Feministisch nein: no feminist theory or method and no structural gender critique.

analysis.notes: Other_Axis: marital or relationship status and household composition, analysed through the 'Really Single' model and the broad cohabitation definition. Gender is coded from the own survey with women's shelters on digital exclusion. Religion appears only as a co-mentioned proxy ground and is not coded. Intersectional is not coded, since intersectional discrimination is named in background and recommendations without a result that depends on a combination of axes. Harm types: Direct_Discrimination through citizenship and foreign-affiliation inputs of the 'Model Abroad', Indirect_Discrimination through apparently neutral household, residency and income inputs acting as proxies and through digital-only access, Exclusionary_Norms through dominant-group norms of household and family embedded in the models and the digital-only default. Stereotyping of foreigners as fraud-prone is argued as a political narrative rather than a system output and is left uncoded. No group-level quality difference could be measured because demographic data was denied, so Disparate_Performance is not coded. Mitigation: proposed ban on citizenship and foreign-affiliation inputs (Pre_Processing) and proposed caseworker training, impact assessments, audits, transparency, independent oversight and non-digital access (Organisational_Process). UDK's equalisation of true positive rates is reported and criticised, not presented as an evaluated mitigation. Gender is treated through women in crisis centres without a definition or recognisable understanding; the glossary enumeration of sex, gender identity and intersex status is a legal list that the analysis does not follow. Theory references: structural discrimination and othering frame the treatment of bias.

evidence.snippet: Machine learning (ML) has been increasingly used in highstake applications such as loans, criminal sentencing, and hiring decisions

analysis.notes: Survey and taxonomy of intersectional fairness notions and mitigation in ML. Gender and race are the worked axes (Figure 1, Black women example); disability, religion, socioeconomic status appear in single cited works or dataset tables. Harm types structuring the synthesis: accuracy and worst-case performance gaps of intersectional subgroups (Disparate_Performance) and outcome-ratio notions derived from the 80 percent disparate-impact rule (Indirect_Discrimination by the YMABYPKF anchor); the survey itself does not classify direct versus indirect discrimination. Mitigation stages from the taxonomy: dataset coverage for intersectional groups (Pre_Processing), in-processing DRO, adversarial reweighting and auditing games (In_Training), multicalibration boosting and prediction flipping (Post_Processing). Evaluated is a synthesised status from reported experimental results of cited methods, not an own experiment. Gender is handled as a categorical attribute ('male/female for a binary gender'). Feministisch ja rests on Crenshaw's intersectionality as the core concept; Gender teilweise because gender is one component axis of an intersectional fairness survey. AI Agent Review: Organisational_Process is added for the recommended involvement of diverse stakeholders in designing fairness notions (sections 2.7 and 6). Binary_Categorical with Intersectional follows the survey own examples, which use female and male as fixed categories combined with race without examining the setting.

analysis.notes: Survey and taxonomy of intersectional fairness notions and mitigation in ML. Gender and race are the worked axes (Figure 1, Black women example); disability, religion, socioeconomic status appear in single cited works or dataset tables. Harm types structuring the synthesis: accuracy and worst-case performance gaps of intersectional subgroups (Disparate_Performance) and outcome-ratio notions derived from the 80 percent disparate-impact rule (Indirect_Discrimination by the YMABYPKF anchor); the survey itself does not classify direct versus indirect discrimination. Mitigation stages from the taxonomy: dataset coverage for intersectional groups (Pre_Processing), in-processing DRO, adversarial reweighting and auditing games (In_Training), multicalibration boosting and prediction flipping (Post_Processing). Evaluated is a synthesised status from reported experimental results of cited methods, not an own experiment. Gender is handled as a categorical attribute ('male/female for a binary gender'). evidence.snippet: In terms of predictive AI, in the housing sector, for example, we have seen how automated tenant screening 'services' rely on eviction records, arrest records, and credit scores in order to rate tenants on their predicted ability to pay rent.

analysis.notes: Conceptual paper that rearticulates the seven data feminism principles for AI research and proposes two further principles (environment, consent); the appendix calls it primarily a literature review and theory contribution, coded Konzept because the principles form a framework. Other_Axis: colonial Global North/Global South position, argued in Principle 7 (labour hierarchy) and 5.1 (environmental impact). Harm types: Exclusionary_Norms for the gender binary operationalised in AI research (4.3), Erasure for missing data on groups and the erasure of trans and non-binary people (4.1, 4.3), Indirect_Discrimination for tenant screening on eviction records, arrest records and credit scores that disproportionately impacts people of color (4.1); harms such as Gender Shades, LAION misogyny or anti-Muslim LLM bias are cited from other work and left uncoded. Mitigation: collection of missing data on underrepresented people (Pre_Processing) and participatory methods, AI education, regulation and collective action (Organisational_Process), all proposed. Bias is not determined in a sentence of its own; the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame (Implicit_Only). Fairness nein: the paper frames its argument as justice and power, not as algorithmic fairness criteria or metrics. AI Agent Review: Generative_KI is teilweise because the work addresses AI research in general and treats generative models as one recurring strand beside predictive AI ('These evaluations are necessary for both generative and predictive AI'). AN_Bias_Definition is Implicit_Only because the adopted definition in Principle 1 determines power, not bias, discrimination or unfairness, and the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame only. The intersectional bias-axis passage of Principle 1 and the status-quo passage of Principle 2 for Exclusionary_Norms were added from the other track.

evidence.snippet: SyRI was an AI-driven system used by the Dutch government to predict and identify individuals at risk of committing fraud in social welfare programs.

analysis.notes: Gegenstand ist die EU-KI-Verordnung, keine Aufgabe der Berufspraxis (AN_Task None). AN_Population Not_SW_Specific, die Sozialhilfe erscheint nur im Fallbeispiel SyRI. Achsen aus der eigenen Analyse: Gender, trans und nicht-binaere Identitaeten (Sexual_Orientation_Identity), Rassifizierung und sozioökonomische Lage im SyRI-Beispiel, Intersectional ueber die Verschraenkung von Race und Einkommen. Exclusionary_Norms: maennliche Normen und Binaritaet in Recht und Daten; Stereotyping: eigenes Beispiel Google Translate. Indirect_Discrimination: in der eigenen feministischen und intersektionalen Fallanalyse von SyRI fuehren historische Daten und Einkommen als scheinbar neutrale Kriterien zur Markierung fuer Betrugsermittlungen in der Sozialhilfe. Arbeitsmarkt- und Gesundheitsfaelle sind zitierte Faelle und bleiben uncodiert. Massnahmen vorgeschlagen: Gender Impact Assessment, intersektionale Bias-Audits, diverse Pruefteams, Beteiligung Betroffener (Organisational_Process) sowie diverse Datensaetze und Pruefung der Trainingsdaten (Pre_Processing). Gender wird nicht in einem eigenen Satz bestimmt, das Verstaendnis folgt aus Queer Theory, sozialer Konstruktion und Intersektionalitaet. Bias wird strukturell gerahmt, ohne eigene Bestimmung. Review: Gender-Definition Implicit_Only, weil das Werk Geschlecht in keinem eigenen Satz bestimmt, sein Verstaendnis aber aus Queer Theory, intersektionalem Feminismus und der Rede von der sozialen Konstruktion erkennbar ist.

analysis.notes: Systematic review of 67 social work AI articles with a proposed Unified Model of Artificial Intelligence Enhanced Social Work along Staub-Bernasconi's triple mandate. Child welfare is the dominant practice area of the reviewed literature (RQ1a), while the model addresses social work in general, so AN_Population is General_Social_Work. Bias axes: indigenous peoples, younger people and the poor appear only as an enumeration of cited under- or over-represented groups, so None. Harm types: the synthesis theme Data and Algorithmic Injustice names exclusion, invisibility, stigmatisation and discrimination as cited consequences without structuring them as harm types, so None. AN_Task: decision support and predictive risk assessment (profession level), text mining for social work research, and agency resource allocation and data exchange (Administration). Mitigation proposals: inclusive data sets (Pre_Processing) and governance, oversight, participation, training and interdisciplinary teams (Organisational_Process). Bias is not defined; its understanding follows the human-rights principle of nondiscrimination. AI Agent Review: AN_Harm_Types None. The synthesis theme 'Data and Algorithmic Injustice' is a section of the review, but it is organised as injustice in general and lists consequences (exclusion, injustice, prejudices, stigmatization and discrimination, invisibility) each taken from a cited study; no harm type structures the synthesis as a section, table row or coded category, and the groups concerned stand in an enumeration that also leaves AN_Bias_Axes at None.

analysis.notes: Interviewstudie (25 Teilnehmende) mit vorab erzeugten ChatGPT-Antworten auf vier Prompts, in denen person durch man, woman, non-binary person ersetzt wird. Prompts dienen als Forschungsinstrument und als vorgeschlagene Test-Suite; die Ersetzung des Personenbegriffs ist keine Technik der Prompt-Report-Familien, daher AN_Prompt_Techniques None. Sexual_Orientation_Identity codiert, weil nicht-binäre und trans Personen als eigene Analysegruppe geführt werden (Geschlechtsidentität); das Werk nennt die Achse gender, daher beide Werte. Schadensarten aus der eigenen Output-Analyse (3.1) und den Interviewbefunden (4.6.2): Stereotyping, cis-zentrischer Default (Exclusionary_Norms), Reduktion nicht-binärer Figuren auf Identitätskämpfe (Misrepresentation). Tonunterschiede nicht als Disparate_Performance codiert (Codebuch 1.4.1), wahrgenommene Genauigkeit gleich über Gruppen. Maßnahmen nur vorgeschlagen: diversere Trainingsdaten und Co-Design bei der Datenkuratierung (Pre_Processing), Rückfragen des Modells bei vagen Prompts (Intra_Processing, 5.2.2), Co-Design, Prompt-Test-Suite und Echtzeit- sowie Community-Bias-Auditing (Organisational_Process). Grounded Theory und reflexive thematische Analyse sind Methoden, keine Theorie, die Gender oder Bias rahmt.

analysis.notes: UNESCO reference framework of twelve AI competency blocks for school students (four aspects by three progression levels) with curricular goals, pedagogical methods, learning environments and assessment items. Inclusivity is one of five key principles with its own section (2.4), hence Diversitaet ja. Bias enters as the non-discrimination principle, as anti-bias measures within section 2.4, the data biases lab and the competency to critique AI-amplified biases; it recurs as learning content beside privacy, human agency and environmental sustainability and is not the framework's central contribution, hence Bias_Ungleichheit teilweise. AN_Bias_Axes None: gender, ethnicity, culture, ability, socio-economic status and language appear only in enumerations of bias types or disaggregation variables. AN_Harm_Types None: no harm mechanism is established for the framework's own object. AN_Mitigation_Stage: Pre_Processing (representative data, data engineering to remove identifiable biases in the data biases lab), In_Training (anti-discrimination and discrimination-free training methods), Organisational_Process (public validation before recommending AI tools, inclusive testing and auditing); all are recommended as curricular content or policy, hence Proposed. AN_Bias_Definition Implicit_Only. AN_Gender_Definition and AN_Gender_Understanding Not_Applicable: gender occurs only in enumerations. AN_Population Not_SW_Specific: school students in general education. AN_Task None: AI is the learning object of a school curriculum; students' own use of AI tools to practise writing is learning activity, not a task of professional practice, and AI-supported assessment by teachers appears only as a supplementary outlook in section 5.8. School teaching lies outside Teaching_Further_Education, which addresses professionals. AN_Prompting_Role None: prompts appear only in a privacy assessment item.

analysis.notes: DR.GAP builds a system prompt from bias-revealing demonstrations (ICL) and step-by-step syllogistic reasoning (Thought_Generation), verified and iteratively refined by the reference model (Self_Criticism), with the persona 'You are a fair and impartial assistant' (Role_Persona). Disparate_Performance rests on the measured accuracy gap between masculine and feminine pronoun texts (Delta G) and the resolution bias in VLMs; Stereotyping on gender-stereotypical associations in reasoning. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit rests on the adopted technical metrics (AccGap, Delta G). Binary gender stated in Limitations and Ethics Statement. AI Agent Review: Exclusionary_Norms is not coded; the male-pronoun default appears in Appendix B only as a hedged explanation of the resolution bias ("This bias may arise because ... the models tend to default to using male pronouns"), not as a result or argument the work establishes.

evidence.term: These technologies have caused numerous harms to queer people, including privacy
evidence.snippet: These technologies have caused numerous harms to queer people, including privacy violations, censoring and downranking queer content, exposing queer people and spaces to harassment by making them hypervisible, deadnaming and outing queer people.

analysis.notes: Fallstudie der Organisation Queer in AI mit eigenen Mitglieder- und Empfängerbefragungen. Die in Abschnitt 2 gelisteten AI-Schäden (Outing, Hassrede, Zensur) sind zitiert; die eigene Analyse betrifft den Ausschluss queerer Menschen aus AI-Forschung, Konferenzen und Publikationswesen. Bias-Achsen, die die eigene Analyse der Teilhabebarrieren entwickelt: gender and sexual orientation (trans und nicht-binäre Personen als eigene Kategorien, Deadnaming), Einkommen (Bewerbungsgebühren, low-income scholars), Global South und Visa (Nationality_Migration), Behinderung und Neurodivergenz, Verstärkung bei intersecting identities. Race_Ethnicity erscheint nur in Demografie- und Reichweitenangaben, Kaste nur in einer Aufzählung (class or caste) und einem Paneltitel; beide bleiben uncodiert. Schadensarten aus eigenen Beobachtungen: exklusive Geschlechtsabfragen und Klarnamenzwang bei Konferenzregistrierung (Exclusionary_Norms), Chat-Software blockiert queere Begriffe (Erasure). Evaluated beschränkt sich auf die organisatorischen Maßnahmen der Organisation (Stipendienprogramm, Workshops, Konferenzleitfaden, Name-Check-Tool), deren Wirkung das Werk nach eigener Angabe bewertet (assess the organization's impact) und mit Befragungsergebnissen und Adoptionsstand berichtet, darunter das gemischte Ergebnis relatively modest adoption; es handelt sich um Maßnahmen gegen Ausschluss aus der AI-Forschung, nicht um technische Bias-Mitigation. Kein ausdrückliches Gender- oder Bias-Verständnis formuliert, Umfragekategorien führen nicht-binäre und weitere Geschlechter.

evidence.term: This paper evaluates a methodological approach to make addressing AI bias more a
evidence.snippet: This paper evaluates a methodological approach to make addressing AI bias more accessible by incorporating a training component on AI bias in a Co-C process with vulnerable and marginalized participant groups.

evidence.snippet: Participatory design (PD) and co-creation (Co-C) approaches to building Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems have become increasingly popular exercises for ensuring greater social inclusion and fairness in technological transformation by accounting for the exp

evidence.snippet: In the toolkit, AI system creators can run existing and new methods to quantify bias for multi-attribute and multimodal data, including preliminary assessment during design and continuous re-evaluation during maintenance.

evidence.snippet: The toolkit offers a user interface to run methods for tackling three critical challenges: bias contained within the MLtraining data of AI components, AI-induced bias that could take the form of spurious correlations (e.g., using postal codes as a proxy of rac

evidence.snippet: In this regard, Donna Activa Forum (DAF), the civil society partner of the MAMMOth project working with under-served women, adapted the material to include examples related to gender biases-something the participants of the workshop could relate to.

evidence.term: DAF added an example based on generative AI queries on the responsibilities of f
evidence.snippet: DAF added an example based on generative AI queries on the responsibilities of fathers and mothers that reproduced outdated and stereotypical gender roles.

evidence.term: In the Co-C workshops, data collection was carried out based on participants' ev
evidence.snippet: In the Co-C workshops, data collection was carried out based on participants' evaluation of three use cases in which AI bias can have a significant impact-financial decisions, e.g., loan applications; biometric identity verification, e.g., automated passport c

evidence.term: Surveys were also conducted amongst communities of vulnerable users recruited th
evidence.snippet: Surveys were also conducted amongst communities of vulnerable users recruited through local civil society organizations involved in the project, including women at risk of social exclusion, e.g., ethnic minority and domestic violence victims, migrants, and rec

analysis.notes: Reflective empirical account of the co-creation workshops of the Horizon Europe MAMMOth project with marginalised groups (women at risk of social exclusion, young people, ethnic minorities, migrants, LGBTQI+ early career researchers), each opened by a training module on AI bias, feeding user and research requirements of an AI bias toolkit. Mitigation Demonstrated: the training within co-creation was applied and is reported only through facilitator and participant reflections, without a completed assessment of an effect on AI bias, although the work calls its approach an evaluation. AN_Task Other_Task: AI-based home loan decisions, biometric identity verification and academic citation search as use cases, outside social work. AN_Bias_Axes: Gender through the training examples added by DAF (generative AI answers on fathers and mothers, gendered job endings in Google Translate, Section 5.1); Religion and Physical_Appearance through the ranked facial attributes for identity verification (hijabs and turbans, piercings and tattoos, Section 4.1). Race_Ethnicity stays uncoded: postal codes as proxy of race appear only as a parenthetical example of a toolkit challenge (Section 4) and the participant consensus that white males benefit most from credit scoring is a single reported perception (Section 4.2); the enumeration 'gender, age, ethnic origin, and sexual orientation' and the participant groups are not coded either. AN_Harm_Types: Stereotyping from the gender-role examples demonstrated in the training, Indirect_Discrimination from the proxy bias the project's own toolkit is built to address. Gender is treated through examples only, without a stated or recognisable understanding, hence Absent and Unclear. AN_Theory_Reference Yes: critical and social-justice perspectives on participatory design (power relations, 'box-ticking', ethics-washing) frame the treatment of AI bias and training; boundary between framing tradition and methodological label. Soziale_Arbeit teilweise: participants include recipients of social protection services and domestic violence victims recruited via civil society organisations, but no social work practice is addressed. The Markdown conversion duplicates and scrambles parts of Sections 4.3 to 5.3; all quotes come from coherent passages.
